title: PT Senior Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) Subject Matter Ex
description:
Requisition Number: 30700

Required Travel: 11 - 25%

Employment Type: Part Time/Hourly/Non-Exempt

Anticipated Salary Range: $148,275.00 - $175,000.00

Security Clearance: TS/SCI

Level of Experience: Senior HI

This opportunity resides with All-Domain Operations (ADO), a business group within HII’s Mission Technologies division. All-Domain Operations comprises multi-domain operations, platforms and logistics, and intelligence operations.

HII designs, develops, integrates and manages the sensors, systems and other assets necessary to support integrated ISR operations and accelerated decision-making. With data fusion and mission management capabilities for the Department of Defense, the combatant commands and the intelligence community, HII advances the mission around the globe.

Leadership at HII – Mission Technologies
HII’s Leadership Capability Framework defines the standard of excellence expected of all leaders across Mission Technologies. Leaders are accountable for modeling these capabilities and building them within their teams:

  • Know & Grow Your People – Develop talent, empower teams, and build an inclusive environment.
  • Build Relationships – Strengthen trust, collaboration, and cross-functional partnerships.
  • Take Ownership – Drive accountability, execution excellence, and results.
  • Customer First – Anticipate mission needs and deliver value to our partners.
  • Shape the Future – Inspire innovation and align work with strategic priorities.
  • Act with Urgency – Make informed decisions and move with purpose.

These capabilities define how leaders inspire teams, deliver results, and shape the future of Mission Technologies.

Summary

HII Mission Technologies is seeking a highly experienced part-time Senior Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) Subject Matter Expert (SME) to support government customers, operational planning efforts, business development initiatives, and proposal activities. The successful candidate will serve as a trusted advisor providing strategic, operational, and technical expertise related to ISR operations, aviation mission planning, airborne sensor employment, and multi-agency mission integration.

This position is ideal for a senior aviation and ISR professional with extensive experience leading complex ISR operations, supporting Combatant Commands, integrating multi-platform collection capabilities, and advising senior government and industry stakeholders across Department of War (DoW), NASA or Service Lab, and international mission environments.

What You Will Do

  • Serve as a senior ISR advisor supporting government customers and internal stakeholders on ISR planning, mission execution, operational integration, and capability development.
  • Lead the assessment, prioritization, and integration of ISR collection requirements to ensure alignment between mission objectives and available platform capabilities.
  • Provide operational expertise supporting CONUS and OCONUS ISR missions across Combatant Commands, including SOUTHCOM, AFRICOM, CENTCOM, and other mission areas.
  • Advise on the employment of airborne ISR platforms, sensors, radar systems, telemetry capabilities, and mission systems in support of intelligence collection and operational objectives.
  • Support the development of Concepts of Operations (CONOPS), operational plans, annexes, appendices, and mission planning products for both steady-state and contingency operations.
  • Provide subject matter expertise for proposal development, capture activities, technical solution development, and customer engagement efforts.
  • Collaborate with military services, Combatant Commands, interagency organizations, and industry partners to synchronize ISR planning and mission execution.
  • Develop and recommend operational security (OPSEC), signature management, and risk mitigation strategies to protect mission effectiveness and sensitive activities.
  • Participate in working groups, planning conferences, and governance forums focused on ISR modernization, aviation operations, range operations, and mission integration.
  • Provide assessments and recommendations related to ISR capabilities, platform utilization, emerging technologies, and operational effectiveness.
  • Represent HII at customer engagements, conferences, workshops, and industry events as a recognized ISR and aviation expert.
  • Travel as required to support customer missions, operational assessments, planning activities, and business development objectives.
  • Perform other duties as assigned in support of organizational and mission requirements.

What We Are Looking For

  • 8 years relevant progressive experience with Bachelors in related field; 6 years relevant progressive experience with Masters in related field; or High School Diploma or equivalent and 12 years relevant progressive experience.
  • 20+ years of progressive experience supporting aviation operations, ISR missions, flight operations, intelligence activities, or related defense programs.
  • Demonstrated expertise planning, managing, and executing ISR operations in complex operational environments.
  • Experience supporting DoW, Combatant Commands, Special Operations Forces, intelligence organizations, or interagency mission partners.
  • Extensive knowledge of ISR collection methodologies, airborne sensor systems, mission planning processes, and intelligence operations.
  • Experience integrating ISR requirements across tactical, operational, and strategic levels.
  • Proven ability to advise and brief senior military leaders, government officials, and industry executives.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience leading cross-functional teams supporting operational missions, intelligence collection, or aviation programs.
  • Valid U.S. Passport and ability to travel domestically and internationally.
  • Clerance: Ability to obtain and maintain a Secret security clearance.

Preferred: Bonus Points For...

  • Bachelor's degree in a related field and 15+ years of relevant experience, Master's degree and 13+ years of relevant experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Clearance: Active Top Secret/SCI security clearance.
  • Experience supporting NASA or Service Lab, Joint, Combatant Command, or interagency operations.
  • Business development, capture management, and proposal support experience within the federal contracting environment.
  • Hands-on experience operating, deploying, integrating, or sustaining airborne ISR platforms and mission systems in direct support of a USG Agency or DoW Agency.
  • Experience supporting RDT&E programs, flight test activities, or test range operations.
  • Familiarity with intelligence community tools and sensors, ISR enterprise architectures, and mission planning systems.
  • Knowledge of emerging ISR technologies, sensor fusion, multi-domain operations, and advanced intelligence collection concepts.
  • Prior military aviation, ISR, intelligence, or special operations experience strongly desired.

The listed salary range for this role is intended as a good faith estimate based on the role's location, expectations, and responsibilities. When extending an offer, HII's Mission Technologies division takes a variety of factors into consideration which include, but are not limited to, the role's function and a candidate's education or training, work experience, and key skills.

Meet HII’s Mission Technologies Division
Our team of more than 7,000 professionals worldwide delivers all-domain expertise and advanced technologies in service of mission partners across the globe. Mission Technologies is leading the next evolution of national defense – the data evolution - by accelerating a breadth of national security solutions for government and commercial customers. Our capabilities range from C5ISR, AI and Big Data, cyber operations and synthetic training environments to fleet sustainment, environmental remediation and the largest family of unmanned underwater vehicles in every class. Find the role that’s right for you. Apply today. We look forward to meeting you.

To learn more about Mission Technologies, click here for a short video:

HII is more than a job - it’s an opportunity to build a new future. We offer competitive benefits such as best-in-class medical, dental and vision plan choices; wellness resources; employee assistance programs; Savings Plan Options (401(k)); financial planning tools, life insurance; employee discounts; paid holidays and paid time off; tuition reimbursement; as well as early childhood and post-secondary education scholarships. Bonus/other non-recurrent compensation is occasionally offered for qualified positions, and if applicable to this role will be addressed by the recruiter at the screening phase of application.

Why HII
We build the world’s most powerful, survivable naval ships and defense technology solutions that safeguard our seas, sky, land, space and cyber. Our workforce includes skilled tradespeople; artificial intelligence, machine learning (AI/ML) experts; engineers; technologists; scientists; logistics experts; and business administration professionals.

Recognized as one of America’s top large company employers, we are a values and ethics driven organization that puts people’s safety and well-being first. Regardless of your role or where you serve, at HII, you’ll find a supportive and welcoming environment, competitive benefits, and valuable educational and training programs for continual career growth at every stage of your career.

Together we are working to ensure a future where everyone can be free and thrive.
All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, physical or mental disability, age, or veteran status or any other basis protected by federal, state, or local law.

Reasonable accommodations are considered on a case-by-case basis. Please note that only those inquiries concerning a request for reasonable accommodation will be responded to from this email address. Additionally, you may also call 1-844-849-8463 for assistance. Press #3 for HII Mission Technologies.

title: Associate Editor, Delacorte Press – Licensed Publishing (Open to Remote) (New Yo
description:
Company Description


Penguin Random House is the leading adult and children's publishing house in North America, the United Kingdom and many other regions around the world. In publishing the best books in every genre and subject for all ages, we are committed to quality, excellence in execution, and innovation throughout the entire publishing process: editorial, design, marketing, publicity, sales, production, and distribution. Our vibrant and diverse international community of nearly 300 publishing brands and imprints include Ballantine Bantam Dell, Berkley, Clarkson Potter, Crown, DK, Doubleday, Dutton, Grosset & Dunlap, Little Golden Books, Knopf, Modern Library, Pantheon, Penguin Books, Penguin Press, Penguin Random House Audio, Penguin Young Readers, Portfolio, Puffin, Putnam, Random House, Random House Children's Books, Riverhead, Ten Speed Press, Viking, and Vintage, among others. More information can be found at


Job Description


Delacorte Press, an imprint of Random House Children’s Books, is seeking an Associate Editor to join its editorial team and support our growing licensed publishing program.

Home to a long history of bestselling and award-winning books, Delacorte is a close-knit, highly collaborative team that believes the best publishing comes from working together. We are passionate about our books and authors, generous with ideas, and invested in one another’s success and we’re looking for a colleague who is excited to contribute to that team culture.

Delacorte’s young adult licensed publishing list includes an exciting and expanding range of properties and publishing partnerships, including Disney, Marvel, Lucas, 20th Century Studios, and Warner Brothers. The program encompasses both licensor-driven publishing and original, in-house developed projects, such as Once Upon a Snowfall by Lydia Gregovic and MJ Loves Spider-Man by Emma Lord.

The Associate Editor will manage a selection of licensed publishing projects, identifying viable licensor-developed titles and working with our team and the licensor to tailor them for our list. They will also identify and develop new publishing opportunities and acquire select projects. Working closely with authors, agents, licensors, and colleagues across Design, Production, Marketing, Publicity, and Sales, this role combines hands-on editorial work, acquisitions, creative development, and project management.

The ideal candidate is a creative and highly organized editor with strong commercial instincts who thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment. They should be excited by the challenge of finding fresh ways to translate established characters, worlds, and franchises into compelling books for young readers while managing multiple projects, stakeholders, approvals, and evolving schedules.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage assigned licensed publishing projects from manuscript development through publication, providing thoughtful editorial feedback and creative direction while ensuring projects meet both Delacorte’s editorial standards and licensor requirements.
  • Identify, develop, and acquire select new projects with an eye toward commercial opportunities, emerging trends, and properties with strong potential in the MG and YA marketplace.
  • Develop original publishing concepts within licensed worlds, including identifying formats, story opportunities, and potential authors and creators.
  • Evaluate proposals and manuscripts and participate in acquisitions discussions.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with authors, agents, licensors, creators, and other external partners, serving as a key liaison throughout the publishing process.
  • Manage licensor submissions, feedback, and approvals while maintaining detailed project schedules and navigating evolving deadlines.
  • Partner closely with Design, Production, Marketing, Publicity, and Sales on positioning and publication plans.
  • Manage retail-exclusive editions and paperback conversions, including the development and approval of new editorial content and design elements.
  • Identify opportunities within the backlist for refreshed, repackaged, or updated editions tied to cultural moments, franchise activity, or renewed consumer interest.
  • Contribute to the strategic growth of Delacorte’s licensed publishing program, identifying opportunities to expand and strengthen the list.

Qualifications


  • 3+ years editorial experience in trade publishing, with experience independently managing books or comparable publishing projects through the editorial and production process.
  • Strong editorial judgment and the ability to provide substantive and line-level editorial feedback.
  • Excellent organizational and project-management skills, with demonstrated ability to manage a large and shifting workload and multiple simultaneous deadlines.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.

title: Software Product Engineer
description:
We are currently looking for a Software Product Engineer for a 100% remote position on a large federal government project. This role will lead the design and development of complex systems that automate complex workflows, support data-driven decision-making, and enhance healthcare technology platforms.

The ideal candidate would be a highly experienced engineer with deep expertise in designing scalable cloud-based architectures and building production-grade AI applied solutions. This role will collaborate closely with engineering teams, product stakeholders, and technical leadership to translate complex concepts into secure, reliable, and scalable solutions.

Essential Functions:

  • Design and build event-driven, data-intensive backend services in Node.js / TypeScript, using cloud native solutions such Amazon Aurora (PostgreSQL), ECS and SQS to support AI workloads at scale.
  • Decompose complex healthcare and AI workflows into a microservices architecture — defining clear service boundaries and data ownership, designing inter-service communication across synchronous REST and asynchronous messaging (SQS/event-driven) patterns, and delivering independently deployable, loosely coupled services that scale and fail independently.
  • Drive a test-driven development (TDD) practice across the team — writing tests before implementation, maintaining strong coverage across unit, integration, and contract tests, and using the test suite to guide design, prevent regressions, and ensure the reliability of AI-enabled services in a regulated environment.
  • Develop AI pipelines that process structured and unstructured data to support intelligent decision systems.
  • Design and implement scalable AI-enabled systems and services that support mission-critical healthcare platforms.
  • Design cloud-native architectures and distributed systems that support AI-driven applications.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to translate product requirements and research concepts into deployable solutions.
  • Take on additional tasks and responsibilities as needed to support team objectives and ensure the success of the project.

Required Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, or a related technical discipline.
  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, including significant experience designing and deploying AI-enabled systems in production environments.
  • Strong hands-on engineering experience with React and Node.js /TypeScript, building production-grade services, REST APIs, and integrations.
  • Hands-on experience with AI-assisted development tools such as Cursor, GitHub Copilot, OpenAI Codex, or Claude Code, with a proven ability to leverage these tools to accelerate development, improve productivity, and enhance code quality.
  • Hands-on experience with AWS data and messaging services, to build event-driven, data-intensive services that support AI workloads.
  • Experience designing and developing microservices, REST APIs, and distributed systems supporting AI workloads.
  • Demonstrated practice of test-driven development (TDD) and automated testing (unit, integration, and contract tests) to ensure reliability and maintainability of production services.
  • Experience implementing CI/CD pipelines, containerized deployments, and DevOps practices for scalable AI systems.
  • Strong problem-solving abilities and experience troubleshooting complex distributed systems.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to guide technical discussions and influence engineering decisions.

Additional Qualifications:

  • Experience building AI solutions within regulated environments such as healthcare or federal government systems.
  • Familiarity with FHIR, HL7, or healthcare interoperability standards.
  • Experience with AI orchestration frameworks, agent-based architecture, or intelligent automation systems.
  • Experience with relational data modeling and performance tuning on PostgreSQL / Amazon Aurora.
  • Experience building asynchronous, message-driven workflows using Amazon SQS (or comparable queueing systems) and object storage with Amazon S3.
  • Experience with container technologies such as Docker or Kubernetes.
  • Experience supporting projects within the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).
  • Ability to obtain a U.S. government clearance.

DPCG is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to hiring and developing the most qualified individuals based on merit, experience, and business needs, without regard to any protected status under applicable law.

title: PATIENT ACCOUNT REP II CORPORATE
description:

Full Time, 80 Hours Per Pay Period, Day Shift

Covenant Health is the region’s top-performing healthcare network with 10 hospitals, outpatient and specialty services, and Covenant Medical Group, our area’s fastest-growing physician practice division. Quality

Serving the Customer

  • Communicate effectively with patients/public, co-workers, physicians, facilities, agencies and/or their offices, and other facility personnel using verbal, nonverbal and written communication skills.
  • Consults and works collaboratively with Supervisors, Co-Workers, Department management, and other facility personnel, effectively performing tasks of position.
  • Attends meetings as required and participates on committees as directed.
  • Perform other duties as assigned or requested.
  • Promotes good public relations for the department ad the facilities, adhering to desired behaviors.
  • Positive resource to peers; approachable and successful at training and development of others.
  • Assists Vice President, Director, Managers and Supervisors on activities and projects, as needed.
  • Supports, models and adheres to the desired behaviors of the KBOS Constitution and Covenant Health for service, which are; take ownership for our mistakes, resolve customer problems on the spot whenever possible, treat all people with respect and kindness, strive to meet or exceed customer expectations, collect and use customer feedback/data to improve processes and service and set an example for accountability and responsiveness: return e-mail and phone calls promptly, assure deadlines are met, keep commitments.

Caring for and Developing Our People

  • Participates freely in intradepartmental quality improvement activities whenever called upon to do so.
  • Provide assistance to new employees.
  • Attends required In-Service training as scheduled.
  • Attends monthly staff meetings and participates in discussions regarding work performance and departmental/facility updates.
  • Supports, models and adheres to desired behaviors of the KBOS Constitution for caring which are; build a trusting environment by listening with a open mind and valuing different opinions; asking questions for understanding and allowing others to speak openly, do not gossip or criticize people behind their back, resolve conflicts, notice and express appreciation for good work and respect differences by listening with a open mind.
  • The KBOS Constitution for developing people which are: commit time to learning and development, help others obtain the information and skills they need to succeed on the job, and utilize training, education and development opportunities.

Using the Community’s Resources Wisely

  • Demonstrates promptness in reporting for and completing work, ensuring follow-through on assigned tasks.
  • Follows protocols as established by the department.
  • Demonstrates initiative in increasing skills and attends training programs as available.
  • Utilizes resources available appropriately, i.e. use of equipment and supplies.
  • Attendance is acceptable per the policy guidelines as defined.
  • Supports, models and adheres to the desired behaviors of the KBOS Constitution for using the community’s resources wisely which are; be aware of cost and quality when making spending decisions, demonstrate a personal commitment to reduce waste, consider the impact on other departments and facilities within Covenant health when making decisions or taking action and ensure that meetings lead to solutions.

None specified; will accept any combination of formal education and/or prior work experience sufficient to demonstrate possession of the knowledge, skill and ability needed to perform the essential tasks of the job, typically such as would be equivalent to a high school diploma or GED. Preference may be given to individuals possessing a HS diploma or GED.

Minimum Experience:

Two to three years’ (2-3) experience in health care is required. Computer experience is required. Knowledge of medical terminology, claims submission, customer service is preferred. Expected to perform adequately within the position after working at least thee to six (3-6) months on the job. Must be familiar with insurance plans and requirements ad collection practices e.g. Fair Debt Credit and Collection Act.

None

Kleinfelder, a Forbes' Top Employer for Engineers in North America, is committed to a people-first culture, technical excellence, and creating opportunities where employees can thrive!

Cultural Resources professionals work on exciting projects involving the identification, preservation, and management of historic, archaeological, and culturally significant sites and resources. They help to ensure that roads, bridges, pipelines, buildings, and other development projects do not accidentally damage important historical sites, archaeological artifacts, cemeteries, or places that have cultural significance to communities and tribes.

Are you an experienced field archaeologist who thrives in the outdoors and enjoys leading teams in remote environments? As an Archaeologist II - Cultural Survey Crew Chief, you will play a critical role in guiding archaeological survey crews across the western United States while ensuring safe, efficient, and high-quality field operations.

This position is ideal for a motivated professional who combines strong archaeological skills with exceptional leadership, logistics coordination, and a commitment to safety. You will serve as the day-to-day leader in the field, directing survey efforts, mentoring crew members, coordinating field logistics, and ensuring compliance with project requirements and cultural resource regulations.

This is an opportunity to advance your archaeology career while exploring some of the most remarkable landscapes in the West. You'll gain leadership experience, work alongside talented professionals, contribute to meaningful resource stewardship, and play a vital role in delivering successful projects while protecting our shared cultural heritage.

If you're ready to lead from the front, prioritize safety, support your team, and make a lasting impact in cultural resource management, we'd love to hear from you.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Field Leadership
  • Lead archaeological survey crews conducting pedestrian surveys, inventories, and cultural resource investigations.
  • Provide daily direction, mentorship, and support to field technicians and junior archaeologists.
  • Promote a positive team culture built on respect, communication, accountability, and collaboration.
  • Ensure field activities are completed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with project objectives.
  • Safety Management
  • Champion a strong safety culture and lead by example in all field activities.
  • Conduct daily safety briefings, hazard assessments, and tailgate meetings.
  • Identify and mitigate risks associated with remote work, rugged terrain, weather conditions, wildlife encounters, and vehicle travel.
  • Ensure compliance with company health and safety procedures and client requirements.
  • Respond appropriately to changing field conditions and emergency situations.
  • Logistics Coordination
  • Coordinate daily field operations, travel arrangements, lodging, vehicle assignments, equipment, and supplies.
  • Monitor crew productivity and survey coverage to meet project schedules and budgets.
  • Manage field data collection, equipment inventories, and project documentation.
  • Communicate regularly with Field Directors, Principal Investigators, and Project Managers regarding project progress and field conditions.
  • Technical Responsibilities
  • Conduct and oversee archaeological surveys in accordance with federal, state, local, and Tribal requirements.
  • Identify, document, photograph, and record archaeological sites, historic properties, and isolated finds.
  • Utilize GPS, GIS, digital data collection platforms, and mapping technologies.
  • Review crew documentation for accuracy, completeness, and quality control.
  • Assist with technical reporting and site documentation as needed.

Position Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Archaeology, Anthropology, or a related field.
  • Completion of an accredited archaeological field school.
  • Minimum of 2-4 years of archaeological survey experience in a Cultural Resource Management (CRM) environment.
  • Experience supervising archaeological field crews and directing daily survey activities.
  • Familiarity with Section 106 compliance and cultural resource management practices.
  • Valid driver's license and ability to travel extensively.
  • Ability to hike long distances carrying field equipment in varying terrain and weather conditions.

Preferred Skills/Experience:

  • Experience leading surveys on federal, state, or private-sector projects.
  • Knowledge of western U.S. archaeology and regional cultural resources.
  • Proficiency with GPS, ArcGIS Field Maps, Survey123, and other digital field technologies.
  • Experience working in remote areas requiring multi-day travel assignments.
  • First Aid/CPR certification and off-road driving experience.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic field environment.

Following an offer, candidates will be required to satisfactorily complete employment reference checks, verification of professional licensure and/or educational credentials, a motor vehicle report (MVR), and a comprehensive background check.

title: Delivery Manager
description:
Ben jij een Delivery Manager die complexe digitale programma’s bij enterprise klanten tot een succes maakt en daarbij de vertrouwde partner van de klant wordt? Als Delivery Manager bij iO ben je eindverantwoordelijk voor de delivery bij een van onze grote klanten, met een groot team dat verdeeld is over meerdere subteams die elk aan een ander product of onderdeel van het klantlandschap werken.

In deze rol ben je de spil tussen klant, teams en directie. Je stuurt een brede technologische delivery aan (UX/UI, analyse, build, infra en maintenance) en een beperktere strategische delivery. Je bewaakt scope, planning, budget en kwaliteit en bouwt tegelijk aan een langdurige relatie met de klant. Je werkt samen met senior management van onze klant: je presenteert aan senior executives, leidt steerco’s, speelt een actieve rol in Quarterly Business Reviews en signaleert commerciële kansen. Je staat er niet alleen voor: een Commercial Lead is verantwoordelijk voor de commerciële ontwikkeling bij de klant (upselling op de huidige scope doe je samen) en een Strategy Lead is de inhoudelijke eindverantwoordelijke voor het strategische deel. Je werkt intensief samen met onze klanten, wanneer zinvol bij de klant op kantoor.

Wat zijn jouw taken als Delivery Manager?

  • Projecten & teams: Eindverantwoordelijk zijn voor de delivery op je projecten en voor je teams (Project Managers, Software Engineers, Functional Analysts en QA Engineers). Je coacht, laat mensen groeien en zorgt dat je delivery organisatie mee evolueert met de klant.

  • Scope, planning & budget: Bewaken van de projectrandvoorwaarden over meerdere complexe projecten, bewuste afwegingen maken tussen scope, tijd, budget en kwaliteit en bijbehorende klantcommunicatie en stakeholder management verzorgen. Je beheert de share of wallet van iO bij de klant.

  • Capaciteit & resources: Strategisch plannen van capaciteit, effortschattingen over teams heen coördineren en resources over projecten heen optimaliseren, met oog voor het welzijn van je teams.

  • Klantrelatie & groei: aanspreekpunt en eerste escalatiepunt voor de klant, klantrelatie beheren via dagelijkse contacten, expectations en verbetertrajecten managen, klantgerichtheid in het team bewaken en samen met de Commercial Lead up- en cross-sell realiseren.

  • Commerciële betrokkenheid: verantwoordelijk voor upsell trajecten vanuit bestaande scope, bijdragen aan sales trajecten bij je klant, de scope laten groeien via vertrouwd advies en investeringsbeslissingen van de klant begeleiden.

  • Governance & rapportering: Rapporteren op managementniveau aan de klant, steerco’s leiden en een actieve rol spelen in de Quarterly Business Reviews.

  • Financiën, risico & kwaliteit: Opvolgen van KPI’s en financiële prestaties van teams en projecten, risico’s op portfolioniveau identificeren, structurele QA-processen uitrollen en na elk project een retrospective houden.

  • Delivery-aanpak & processen: Delivery-aanpakken ontwerpen voor complexe projecten met meerdere teams (waar gepast met een combinatie van methodieken), standaarden neerzetten per projecttype en operationele processen en tooling optimaliseren.

  • Crisismanagement: Leiden van complexe crisissituaties, crisisprotocollen opzetten en de klantrelatie versterken door transparant te blijven onder druk.

  • AI in delivery: Opzetten van AI-tooling voor het delivery team (templates, geautomatiseerde rapportage, projectspecifieke workflows) en collega’s begeleiden in verantwoord en effectief AI-gebruik.

  • Je hebt ruime ervaring met het leiden van grote, complexe digitale projecten of programma’s bij enterprise klanten, bij voorkeur in een agency- of consultancyomgeving.

  • Je hebt technologische delivery in de vingers (UX/UI, analyse, softwarebouw, infrastructuur en onderhoud) en weet de juiste vragen te stellen en de juiste beslissingen te nemen.

  • Je kunt meerdere teams en disciplines aansturen, ook zonder hiërarchische lijn, bouwt high-performing teams en laat mensen groeien.

  • Je beheerst klassieke, agile en hybride werkvormen en combineert ze waar dat past.

  • Je hebt sterk financieel en commercieel inzicht: je bewaakt budgetten, voorspelt afwijkingen tijdig en herkent kansen om waarde toe te voegen.

  • Je bent communicatief uitstekend en kunt aan senior stakeholders rapporteren, steerco’s en QBR’s leiden en complexe situaties vertalen naar duidelijke keuzes en acties.

  • Je blijft kalm en transparant onder druk en neemt de leiding wanneer het spannend wordt.

  • Je bent pragmatisch en hands-on, zoekt actief naar slimmere manieren van werken (waaronder verantwoord gebruik van AI) en vertrekt vanuit de klant met oog voor vertrouwen op lange termijn.

  • Je beheerst het Nederlands en Engels uitstekend.

*Deze vacature staat open voor zowel kandidaten op payroll als freelancers.

description:

Full Time, 80 Hours Per Pay Period, Day Shift

Covenant Medical Group is the employed and managed medical practice organization of Covenant Health, providing comprehensive care across East Tennessee. With more than 300 physicians and advanced practice providers in 20 communities, our team delivers expertise across a broad spectrum of specialties from primary care and walk-in clinics to preventive medicine and advanced surgical and subspecialty services. Position Summary:

Performs complex tasks associated with mammography/breast biopsy/other breast imaging procedures by applying proper ionizing radiation coupled with accurate positioning, compression, and processing techniques to obtain high-quality diagnostic images for interpretation by radiologist. The Mammography Tech is responsible for maintain a safe Breast Center environment at all times.

Responsibilities

  • Performs all duties of Mammography Radiology Technologist. Performs routine screening/diagnostic/ minimally invasive breast imaging procedures through technical expertise in equipment use, positioning and procedure protocols. Follows the Joint Commission procedures regarding medication preparation/usage on patient for minimally invasive breast procedures. Follow policy regarding time out prior to minimally invasive procedures being performed. Obtains and documents pertinent clinical information and technical findings for review by physician for order clarification and follow-through. Follows established processes for supply charging, stock maintenance and vendor ordering. Perform complex tasks associated with the operation of an Accredited Breast Center and related equipment to produce high quality Breast Imaging. Selects appropriate associated equipment/data manipulation to achieve desired results with factors influencing data acquisition. Technically proficient in the operation and quality control aspects of scanning and image recording equipment specific to the assigned work area. Displays independent work skills by capably taking physician orders to completion to include correct patient transport, required clerical skills, physician defined scanning parameters, acquisition, filming and physician interpretation. Practices aseptic/sterile technique and applies universal precautions as appropriate. Applies appropriate infection prevention techniques and processes.
  • Identifies and screens patient. Obtains patient history, completes and verifies accurate consents, informed consent and/or permits as needed. Provide patient instructions/education to obtain desired results, gain cooperation and minimize anxiety during exams. Position patients for mammography/breast biopsies/other breast imaging using immobilization and protective equipment to comply with regulations while applying principles of ALARA to minimize risk to patient, self and others. Position patient and equipment to best demonstrate the anatomic area of interest, respecting the patient’s ability, safety and comfort. Provide for psychological and physical needs of patients for Breast procedures. Proficient in patient assessment and monitoring.
  • Proficient in required data entry, record maintenance and statistical data. Technically proficient in the operation and quality control aspects of scanning and image recording equipment specific to the assigned work area. Maintains patient’s confidential records, reports and files, following established HIPAA guidelines.
  • Provides patients and families with procedural explanation or written documentation of procedure. Responds appropriately and timely to patients, physicians and other customer needs. Coordinates the smooth transition of patients throughout the hospital and other campus locations.

Qualifications

Minimum Education:

None specified; however, must be sufficient to meet the standards for achievement of the below indicated license and/or certification as required by the issuing

Minimum Experience:

Must be registered ARRT (R).

Licensure Requirement:

Must have and maintain ARRT (R) and within 6 months ARRT (M). State licensure in accordance with Tennessee guidelines.

title: SRO Assistant Residential Services Coordinator
description:
Overview

With assistance from the Program Director, the Assistant Residential Services Coordinator assumes primary responsibility for performing and coordinating the services and functions necessary to enhance the resident’s autonomy, quality of life, and recovery process. Carries a caseload of no more than 7 residents.

Why work for DePaul?

  • Make a positive difference in someone's life
  • Supportive work environment
  • We value diversity
  • Opportunity for professional development and career advancement
  • Excellent benefits and competitive wages (see below for details)
  • The pay range for this position is $21.75 - $22.05/hour

Responsibilities

  • With assistance from the Program Director, develops the overall Residential Service Plan with the resident and his or her support network by identifying the individual’s needs and desires in an effort to lead productive and fulfilling lives.
  • Provide teaching, monitoring and recovery oriented supports in accordance with OMH 595 including the following rehabilitative services: Assertiveness / Self-Advocacy Training, Community Integration / Resource Development, Daily Living Skills, Health Services, Medication Management / Training, Parenting Training, Rehabilitative Counseling, Skill Development, Socialization, Substance Abuse Services, Symptom Management.
  • With assistance from the Program Director, ensure that each resident receives comprehensive planning in a person-centered approach for; admission (including the completion of admission notes), on-going recovery-oriented services, and discharge. Ensure that each plan is complete and up to date in accordance with standards of practice and the New York State Office of Mental Health.
  • With assistance from the Program Director, conducts quarterly reviews of the Residential Service Plan with the individual in an effort to ascertain the degree of progress and to make revisions when necessary.
  • Observe, monitor, document, and report resident behaviors as well as their progress in accordance with agency standards.
  • Maintain accurate and timely resident files, including the documentation of progress notes, the updating of service plans, the maintenance of psychiatric and medical records, as well as other pertinent information regarding the resident.
  • Ensures that annual appointments for physicals, eye exams and dental appointments are scheduled. Ensures that transportation is arranged for these appointments (when appropriate). Follows proper guidelines when a resident chooses not to attend / follow through with medical appointment /recommendations.
  • Works collaboratively with the resident’s community service providers to ensure continuity of care (care managers clinical, medical, educational, vocational, and entitlement specialists, etc.). Makes appropriate referrals to these services when needed. This also includes all mandated linkages (Mental Health court, AOT, probation, etc.)
  • Serves as the key liaison between the resident and his / her clinical provider. Contacts the resident’s clinical provider at least monthly to ensure effective monitoring of the individual’s mental health and well-being.
  • Help residents to plan for the purchasing of clothes and other necessities.
  • Works with residents to encourage a healthy connection with family and community ties and to develop new supports and interests.
  • Works with the Intake Director to provide perspective residents with tours and lunch visits as part of the admission process.
  • Respects and maintains resident confidentiality and demonstrates a caring, positive attitude toward all residents (as per respect policy), staff, guests, and service providers.
  • Provide safe transporting of residents when needed.
  • Follow all safety rules and regulations for self, residents, and staff.
  • Performs any other duties necessary for the effective operation of the program.

Qualifications

Needs to meet one of the following three criteria:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a Human Services field
  • Associates degree in a Human Services field plus two (2) years residential experience
  • High School diploma / GED plus four (4) years full-time residential experience

*In addition to the above criteria this position also requires a clean New York State driving record as outlined in DePaul’s personnel policy. Must be at least Eighteen (18) years of age.

Benefits

This position is eligible for the following benefits: Medical Insurance, Dental Insurance, Vision Insurance, Life Insurance, Generous PTO & Paid Holidays, 403B Employer Match, and Employee Discount Programs.

DePaul is an equal opportunity employer that values diversity. All employment is decided based on qualifications, merit and program need.

title: Data Engineer
description:
Overview

Good Things Start Here.

Good things are happening at Berkshire Hathaway GUARD Insurance Companies—an A+ (Superior) rated, nationwide Property & Casualty insurer backed by Berkshire Hathaway. Responsibilities

You will collaborate directly with business leaders to translate questions into curated datasets, intuitive Power BI models, analytic insights and clear narratives that influence decisions.   • Model and publish curated, analysis ready datasets, semantic models in Power BI or analytics delivery that illuminate small commercial metrics.
  • Continuously learn and expand business knowledge to proactively produce automated analytic solutions to business challenges.
  • Design, develop, and maintain scalable ELT/ETL pipelines and lakehouse structures in Microsoft Fabric; Follow platform standards, optimize for performance, reliability, and cost.
  • Follow and implement documentation standards, governance and data quality controls across datasets.
  • Use Azure DevOps (ADO) for CI/CD and version control (branching, pull requests, release pipelines) to harden delivery and improve repeatability.
  • Document technical architecture and workflows to support onboarding and reduce risk
  • Apply best practices in data modeling and engineering to create reusable, high-quality data products.
  • Work in an Agile/Scrum environment, contributing to sprint planning, backlog refinement, and demos.
  • Support development and scaling of data products, BI solutions, and AI-driven use cases across business areas.

Qualifications

Required

  • Hands-on experience in data modeling (conceptual, logical, physical), data engineering, analytics engineering, SQL, and Python
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, IT, or related field
  • 5+ years of data engineering experience, preferably in P&C insurance
  • Experience with Data Mesh (domain ownership and decentralized data products)
  • Strong experience with modern lakehouse platforms (e.g., Microsoft Fabric, Databricks, Snowflake, AWS)
  • Experience building data solutions in cloud environments (Azure preferred; AWS a plus)
  • Familiarity with Azure DevOps (ADO) and CI/CD practices
  • Experience with data transformation, semantic modeling, and BI tools (Power BI, Tableau)
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Experience working in Agile/Scrum environments with product-based delivery
  • Experience delivering end-to-end data, analytics, or AI solutions with business stakeholders
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills

Preferred:

  • Experience with distributed processing frameworks (e.g., Spark)
  • Knowledge of data warehousing concepts and tools
  • Additional programming experience (e.g., Scala)
  • Understanding of data security and compliance
  • Microsoft Fabric certifications (e.g., DP-600, DP-700)
  • Experience with AI agents or multi-agent frameworks for business use cases

Salary Range:

$100,000 – $140,000.

In accordance with applicable pay transparency laws, the above range represents a good-faith estimate. Final compensation will be determined based on factors such as experience, credentials, geographic location, and other considerations permitted by law.

This role may be based out of any of our office locations, including:

Plano, TX, New York, NY, Scottsdale, AZ, Wilkes-Barre, PA

The successful candidate is expected to work in one of our offices 3 days per week and also be available for travel as required.

title: Remote Bilingual Mandarin Customer Experience Specialist
description:
Alignment Health is breaking the mold in conventional health care, committed to serving seniors and those who need it most: the chronically ill and frail. It takes an entire team of passionate and caring people, united in our mission to put the senior first.We have built a team of talented and experienced people who are passionate about transforming the lives of the seniors we serve. description:

This position is responsible to ensure equal opportunity in employment in that all persons are treated equally and on the basis of merit, in decisions regarding selection, placement, promotions, training, work assignments, transfers and other personnel actions.

City: Remote

State: Remote

Job Summary:

The Building Performance & Energy Assessor is responsible for performing facility condition assessments, energy audits, and building performance evaluations for commercial, institutional, municipal, and multifamily properties. This position combines traditional facility assessment services with energy and sustainability consulting, including ASHRAE energy audits, utility benchmarking, building performance analysis, and capital planning support. The Energy & Facility Assessor conducts field assessments, analyzes building systems, develops technical recommendations, and prepares comprehensive reports that help clients improve building performance, reduce operating costs, and support long-term capital and sustainability goals.

Specific Duties & Responsibilities

  • Conducts client-facing on-site assessments and prepares written reports that accurately document assessment findings, including but not limited to:
    • Facility Condition Assessments (FCA)
    • ASHRAE Level I, II, and III Energy Audits
    • Mechanical equipment evaluations
    • Building Energy Management System (BEMS/BAS) diagnostics
    • Accessibility assessments
    • Space utilization planning and analysis
    • Utility benchmarking and energy performance evaluations
    • Other technical services supporting capital planning for commercial, institutional, municipal, and multifamily facilities
  • Performs energy and sustainability consulting services including:
    • Conducting ASHRAE Level I, II, and III Energy Audits.
    • Performing diagnostic evaluations of Building Energy Management Systems (BEMS/BAS) and identifying operational improvement opportunities.
    • Identifying opportunities for energy and water conservation and developing calculations to quantify projected savings and return on investment.
    • Performing utility allowance studies, Statements of Energy Performance (SEP), ENERGY STAR benchmarking, carbon benchmarking, and related building performance analyses.
    • Developing recommendations that support clients' sustainability, ESG reporting, decarbonization, and Net Zero initiatives.
    • Performing building energy modeling using software such as TREAT, eQUEST, DesignBuilder, Wrightsoft, RemRate, Trane TRACE, or comparable energy modeling platforms.
  • There may also be previously prepared building condition survey reports, appraisals, energy studies, benchmarking reports, and accessibility surveys that must be analyzed using specialized technical knowledge.
  • Completes equipment and building component inventories, documenting building systems, operating conditions, and deficiencies.
  • Determines system type, condition, remaining useful life, operational performance, and significant physical deficiencies through visual observations, interviews, utility analysis, and field investigation.
  • Provides planning-level repair, replacement, and energy improvement recommendations with associated cost estimates for inclusion in capital improvement plans.
  • Travel (by Plane, Motor Vehicle, Train) is a significant component of this role, with approximately 50% of work time spent traveling to client sites throughout the United States.

Core Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Performs Facility Condition Assessments, Property Condition Assessments, energy audits, accessibility assessments, mechanical evaluations, space utilization analyses, and other building assessment services based on client-specific scopes of work.
  • Performs physical surveys of accessible building systems, including architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, roofing, and site components.
  • Evaluates building systems to identify deferred maintenance, capital replacement needs, operational deficiencies, and opportunities for improved energy and water efficiency.
  • Collects field data necessary to support lifecycle cost analysis, capital planning, and energy conservation recommendations.
  • Performs utility benchmarking and analyzes historical utility consumption data.
  • Develops energy and water savings calculations to support client decision-making.
  • Reviews building documentation including construction drawings, maintenance records, utility data, repair histories, warranties, and capital improvement records.
  • Prepares comprehensive technical reports that summarize assessment findings, building deficiencies, capital planning recommendations, energy improvement opportunities, benchmarking results, and supporting documentation.
  • Collaborates with internal technical teams to support multidisciplinary assessment projects.
  • Meets productivity, report quality, and client service expectations.
  • Maintains confidentiality of company and client information.
  • Follows all company policies, quality standards, SOPs, and safety requirements.

Skills:

  • Knowledge of Facility Condition Assessments, capital planning, reserve studies, and Asset Management services.
  • Understanding of commercial building systems, including HVAC, electrical, plumbing, building envelope, lighting, and controls.
  • Knowledge of ASHRAE energy auditing methodologies and building performance principles.
  • Familiarity with Building Automation Systems (BAS/BEMS) and building controls.
  • Experience with utility benchmarking, ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager, utility allowance studies, carbon benchmarking, and sustainability reporting.
  • Experience using energy modeling software such as eQUEST, DesignBuilder, TREAT, Trane TRACE, Wrightsoft, RemRate, or comparable platforms.
  • Strong analytical, technical writing, problem-solving, and communication skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, AssetCalc, Quire, and other business-specific software.
  • Ability to operate an electronic tablet for field data collection.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

This job does not have specific supervisory responsibilities.

Education, Certifications & Experience:

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Architecture, Building Science, Construction Management, Energy Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Environmental Science, or a related technical field with a minimum of three (3) years of related experience.

OR

Five (5) years of progressively responsible experience performing facility assessments, energy audits, commissioning, building performance evaluations, or related technical consulting services in lieu of a degree.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Certified Energy Manager (CEM)
  • Building Energy Assessment Professional (BEAP)
  • Existing Building Commissioning Professional (EBCP)
  • Building Commissioning Professional (BCxP)
  • BPI Multifamily Building Analyst
  • LEED Green Associate or LEED AP
  • WELL AP or other sustainability credential

Physical and Environmental Conditions:

While performing the onsite/field duties, the employee is required to:

  • Stand (material part of an 8-hour workday, up to 3 to 4 continuous hours at one time.)

title: Surgical Tech - Operating Room - F/T with Benefits Day
description:
Overview

Our team members are the heart of what makes us better. At Hackensack Meridian Health we help our patients live better, healthier lives — and we help one another to succeed. With a culture rooted in connection and collaboration, our employees are team members. Here, competitive benefits are just the beginning. It’s also about how we support one another and how we show up for our community. Together, we keep getting better - advancing our mission to transform healthcare and serve as a leader of positive change.

Responsibilities

A day in the life of a Surgical Tech at Hackensack Meridian Health includes:

  • Prepares rooms with appropriate instruments, sutures, supplies and equipment necessary for each individual surgical procedure as outlined in the departmental policy and procedure manual; refers to the physician's preference book for special needs, equipment, or instruments of the surgeon performing the scheduled operation.
  • Demonstrates competence in assisting the surgical team during operative procedures.
  • Consistently passes instruments, sponges, sutures, and suction tubes to surgeon and surgical assistants, as requested, in such a manner that the surgeon need not to divert attention from the operating field.
  • Remains alert during procedures and demonstrates an ability to handle unexpected situations with calm efficiency.
  • Follows departmental procedures in: scrubbing, hand drying, gowning, gloving, and observing for contamination and /or breaks in aseptic technique. Demonstrates close attention to details of aseptic technique at all times.
  • Follows aseptic technique when opening sterile supplies and setting-up procedures. Discards any contaminated supplies immediately, according to established written procedures.
  • Demonstrates an awareness of legal responsibilities and the reason for complete accuracy when performing operating room counts (sponge, needle, instruments); knows proper procedure to follow in case of an incorrect count; reports discrepancies and /or corrections immediately.
  • Follows written procedures in accounting for reporting the number of drains and/or packs and their location to the Circulating Nurse.
  • Demonstrates competence in the care of specimens (bacteriological anaerobic and aerobic, frozen sections, pathological, E.E.A. testing, Calculli, Care of limb - post-amputation), and in the accurate recording, labeling, and handling of specimens at all times.
  • Adjusts lights and other equipment as directed by the surgeon or staff nurse: always follows orders carefully and completely; checks on a daily basis assigned O.R. equipment to ensure proper functioning; maintains an awareness of special maintenance procedures; promptly reports any inoperative equipment to the supervisor; inspects the department regularly for proper equipment functions.
  • Keeps operative field in a neat, clean, dry and sterile condition; identifies and immediately reports any breaks in aseptic techniques by self and others; maintains a sterile set-up until the patient has left the operating rooms following operations, including disposal of used linens gloves, instruments, utensils, equipment and waste; cleans instrument tables at the end of each case according to established procedures; autoclaves waste, as necessary. Restocks supplies, as necessary.
  • Follows established procedures in making up special sterile supplies such as: needles, catheters, Penrose drain, cotton balls, etc. sterilizes specific instruments as necessary according to proper sterilization procedures; demonstrates proper wrapping techniques of supplies for sterilization.
  • Follows written procedures for gas and steam sterilization; knows responsibilities and the necessity for chemical and bacteriological monitoring.
  • Ensures comfort and safety for patient; demonstrates an awareness of patient`s fears and apprehension. Supports patients emotionally in the pre-and post-surgical phase. Communicates clearly and tactfully with patients.
  • Assists in transportation of patient as required from bed to operating room. Demonstrates an awareness of patient safety and proper body mechanics.
  • Gowns and gloves other scrubbed personnel, as requested, following strict aseptic procedures at all times.
  • Assists in draping patients for surgical procedures; follows procedures outlined in the departmental manual.
  • Assists in the preparation of patient operative areas according to the need; carefully follows established procedures under the direction of the Operating Room Staff Nurse.
  • Attends O.R. Staff Meeting; attends all JCAHO required in-service education programs yearly; participates in hospital emergency and disaster procedures; knows personal role in case of a fire while on duty.
  • Assists with the orientation of new personnel assigned to O.R.
  • Respond within 30 minutes when on-cal.
  • Other duties and/or projects as assigned.
  • Adheres to HMH Organizational competencies and standards of behavior.

Qualifications

Education, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Required:

  • Satisfactory completion of an approved Operating Room Technician course and/or a graduate of an accredited school of Practical Nursing.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Proficient computer skills that may include but are not limited to Microsoft Office and/or Google Suite platforms.

Education, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Preferred:

  • One year of OR experience

Licenses and Certifications Required:

  • Licensed Practical Nurse or Certified Surgical Technologist.

If you feel that the above description speaks directly to your strengths and capabilities, then please apply today!

Starting Minimum Rate

Minimum rate of $28.28 Hourly

Job Posting Disclosure

HMH is committed to pay equity and transparency for our team members. The posted rate of pay in this job posting is a reasonable good faith estimate of the minimum base pay for this role at the time of posting in accordance with the New Jersey Pay Transparency Act and does not reflect the full value of our market-competitive total rewards package. title: Master Scheduler
description:
SRC, Inc. is currently seeking a Master Scheduler. The selected candidate will fill an upcoming position upon task being awarded. This opportunity supports the Department of War (DoW) in their efforts to identify and defeat hard deeply buried targets (HDBT). This position requires strong communication skills and understanding of project management and military operations. Liaison between manufacturing, testing, requirements and operational organizations for integrating project management reviews, lab and field demonstrations, testing, and development of integrated master schedules (IMS) of end-to-end WMD/HDBT programs. Strong ability to work collaboratively across multidisciplinary government, military and contractor teams.

What You'll Do

  • Assist in schedule forecasting and tracking program efforts to include milestones, test events, deliverables, schedule & review meeting requirements, program management reviews, identify schedule delays or situations that could impact program timelines
  • Facilitate IMS planning sessions, status meetings, and schedule reviews with program stakeholders
  • Assist in planning demonstrations for full-scale weapon delivery testing and tactics development efforts with military requirements
  • Attend weapon delivery and effects testing, assist in the scheduling of logistical preparation of test beds and test sites, and be primary point of contact for onsite coordination with Kirkland AFB
  • Develop schedule graphics, dashboards, and visualizations that communicate program health, execution trends, key milestones, dependencies, and risks.
  • As needed, be able to work in confined spaces low level radiation areas and wear appropriate personal protective equipment (up to level A). Capable of performing work in outdoor areas of heavy construction, confined environments, exposure to wildlife, as needed work in extreme outdoor weather, and drive on hazardous terrain and around structures
  • Collaborate with program managers, technical teams, government stakeholders, and functional leads to ensure schedule integrity and alignment with program objectives.

What You'll Bring

  • Bachelor’s with 4 or more years of experience or 8 years of relevant military, government, or industry training and experience in lieu of degree
  • An Active Top Secret / SCI security clearance (or be eligible at time of application for SCI)
  • Proven experience with military activities, base and range operations
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to produce and present technical deliverables to government stakeholders
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Microsoft Project, OnePager Pro or equivalent scheduling and visualization tools
  • Must be able to prioritize multiple tasks with local organizations and dispersed offices throughout continental United States

Ways to Stand Out

  • Prior experience supporting OSW, DARPA, DTRA, ARL, or service-level acquisition programs
  • PMI Scheduling Professional (PMI-SP), Project Management Professional (PMP) certification, or AACE Planning & Scheduling Professional (AACE PSP)
  • Prior experience with military base operations, tactical and operational planning

What Sets Us Apart?
SRC, Inc., a not-for-profit research and development company, combines information, science, technology and ingenuity to solve “impossible” problems in the areas of defense, environment and intelligence. Across our family of companies, we apply bright minds, fresh thinking and relentless determination to deliver innovative products and services that are redefining possible®. When you join our team, you’ll be a part of something truly meaningful — helping to keep America and its allies safe and strong. You’ll collaborate with more than 1,400 engineers, scientists and professionals — with 20 percent of those employees having served in the military — in a highly innovative, inclusive and equitable work environment. You’ll receive a competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package that includes four or more weeks of paid time off to start, 10 percent employer contribution toward retirement, and 100 percent tuition support.

Total compensation for this role is market competitive. The anticipated salary range for this position based out of Albuquerque, NM is estimated at $88,000 to $110,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s experience, skills, and abilities, geographic location as well as other business and organizational needs. SRC offers competitive benefit options, for more details please visit our website.

description:

JuiceX is a rapidly growing prediction markets exchange. Our company is building the infrastructure to offer a fully compliant, transparent, and innovative marketplace for event driven contracts under U.S. regulatory frameworks.

We are hiring Control Center Analysts to support real-time monitoring and operational oversight of JuiceX’s Exchange.   • Experience working in time-sensitive roles requiring rapid decision-making and escalation

  • Clear written and verbal communication skills

title: IEP Coordinator
company: HEARTSHARE HUMAN SERVICES OF NEW YORK
location: The HeartShare School, 1825 Bath Ave, BKLYN, NY, 11214 - Brooklyn, NY 11214
description:
The IEP Coordinator provides leadership and coordination for the educational and IEP-related functions of the HeartShare Education Center, an NYSED-approved 853 school serving students with disabilities ages 5–22. This position combines IEP coordination, educational programming, curriculum support, instructional guidance, compliance monitoring, and coordination with teachers, related service providers, families, and school districts. The IEP Coordinator serves as a key educational resource to the school community and supports the consistent implementation of students' IEPs and high-quality, individualized educational programming. The position works closely with the Principal/Director of Education to monitor educational quality, address program needs, maintain IEP compliance, and support continuous improvement across the school.

This position has no direct or indirect supervisory responsibility for instructional, clinical, administrative, or support staff. The IEP Coordinator does not conduct employee evaluations, approve personnel actions, assign staff, discipline employees, or manage employee performance. The position provides coordination, monitoring, communication, and technical assistance related to IEP implementation.

Essential Functions and Primary Responsibilities of Position:

IEP Coordination & Compliance

  • Coordinate the school's IEP tracking and monitoring systems, including annual reviews, reevaluations, amendments, and other required timelines.
  • Monitor implementation of IEP recommendations and ensure teachers and appropriate staff have access to current IEP information.
  • Coordinate with CSEs, school districts, families, teachers, related service providers, and other members of the educational team regarding IEPs and student programming.
  • Participate in CSE meetings, annual reviews, program reviews, and other student planning meetings as assigned.
  • Review IEP-related documentation for completeness, accuracy, and compliance.
  • Identify and communicate IEP implementation or compliance concerns to the Principal/Director of Education.
  • Assist with preparation for NYSED monitoring, audits, reviews, and corrective action activities.

Educational Program & Curriculum Support

  • Support the development and implementation of high-quality educational programming across the school.
  • Provide teachers with guidance regarding curriculum, differentiated instruction, IEP goals, accommodations, modifications, and instructional strategies.
  • Review lesson plans, instructional materials, and classroom programming as part of the school's educational quality-monitoring process.
  • Support alignment between curriculum, classroom instruction, student needs, and IEP goals.
  • Assist with development and implementation of school-wide educational initiatives.
  • Identify instructional resources and professional development needs and make recommendations to school leadership.
  • Provide instructional coaching, modeling, consultation, and resources to teachers as appropriate.

Student Programming & Team Collaboration

  • Collaborate with teachers, related service providers, school psychologists, behavior professionals, and other team members to support individualized student programming.
  • Participate in multidisciplinary student support meetings.
  • Assist educational teams in addressing academic, functional, behavioral, communication, social, vocational, and life-skills needs.
  • Support development of educational programming that promotes student engagement, independence, and meaningful outcomes.
  • Assist with transition planning and programming for students preparing for employment, further education, adult services, and increased independence.

Family & School District Relations

  • Serve as a school-based resource to families regarding educational and IEP-related matters.
  • Support communication with families and school districts regarding student programming, IEPs, evaluations, and educational services.
  • Develop and maintain positive working relationships with CSE representatives, school districts, and other educational partners.
  • Assist in addressing questions or concerns related to educational programming in collaboration with school leadership.

Quality Assurance & Documentation

  • Monitor educational programming and documentation for consistency with NYSED requirements, IEPs, and HeartShare standards.
  • Maintain accurate tracking systems and reports related to IEP timelines, educational documentation, and program requirements.
  • Identify trends, gaps, and opportunities for improvement and communicate recommendations to school leadership.
  • Assist with development and implementation of corrective action plans when educational or compliance concerns are identified.
  • Maintain confidentiality and security of student educational records in accordance with applicable requirements.

Professional Development & School Improvement

  • Assist with planning and delivering professional development related to curriculum, instruction, IEP implementation, and special education practices.
  • Support implementation of educational improvement initiatives.
  • Stay current with NYSED requirements, special education practices, and educational trends relevant to the school's student population.
  • Participate in school leadership and HeartShare meetings as assigned.
  • Performs other job-related duties as assigned, consistent with the scope, responsibilities, and level of the position, and in compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and organizational policies.

title: Robotic Process Automation (RPA) Engineer
description:
Overview

Ready to automate the processes that keep the Department of War’s finances running? As FWI’s RPA Engineer on the DA2I program, you’ll design, build, and sustain automation solutions on platforms like UiPath, Automation Anywhere, and Power Automate that make Comptroller business processes faster and more accurate. If you want your automation skills to support a real DoW mission, not just another bot, this is the seat.

FWI is building a team to support the Department of War Comptroller and as an RPA Engineer, you will play a crucial role in designing, developing, and managing RPA solutions across the full automation lifecycle, from requirements analysis through deployment, monitoring, and maintenance, using SQL Server, Python/PySpark, SSIS, PowerShell, and Azure to improve business process efficiency and accuracy.

FWI is expanding rapidly and has been recognized as a 2024, 2025 and 2026 Top Workplace, offering excellent growth opportunities in a collaborative environment.

Work Schedule and Location:

Hybrid: This role is based in Arlington, Virginia and works on a hybrid schedule, typically 1–2 days on site per month, with the balance remote. We are looking for someone in the National Capital Region who can be on site when the mission calls for it, not only on a fixed schedule. Working alongside the government team in person is part of how this role builds the relationships the work depends on.

Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, implement, and manage Robotic Process Automation solutions that improve business process efficiency and accuracy across federal and commercial environments.
  • Support the full RPA lifecycle: requirements analysis, development, testing, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance.
  • Translate business requirements into scalable automation workflows.
  • Integrate automations with enterprise systems.
  • Ensure data integrity and maintain documentation.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders to resolve issues and enhance automation performance.

Qualifications

Required:

  • 3–10 years of directly related experience and a B.A./B.S. or M.A./M.S.
  • 3+ years of experience with major RPA platforms (UiPath, Automation Anywhere, Microsoft Power Automate).
  • Advanced proficiency in programming languages and tools including SQL Server, Python/PySpark, R, C#, SSIS, SSRS, PowerShell, and cloud environments such as Azure.
  • Ability to analyze business processes and translate requirements into automation workflows.
  • Strong independent troubleshooting skills for automation failures, including implementing corrective actions.
