title: Sr. Director, Foundation Operations
description:
Overview

The Sr. Director, Foundation Operations leads the operational systems, processes, controls, and administrative infrastructure that support the Central Health Foundation. Reporting to the Foundation Chief Executive Officer, the Sr. Director serves as the Foundation’s senior operational leader and translates approved strategies and leadership decisions into practical workflows, procedures, systems, controls, and service expectations. The position leads the Foundation’s coordination with Central Health sharedservice partners and represents the Foundation in operational, financial, compliance, technology, procurement, and administrative processes.

The Sr. Director has direct responsibility for Foundation-owned operational functions, including donor and gift administration, pledge and fund accounting coordination, grant accounting and monitoring, donor records, Foundation CRM ownership, Board administration, operating procedures, and related controls and reporting. The position also leads the Foundation’s role in budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, audit readiness, contracts, procurement coordination, and shared-service management. The Sr. Director leads the Foundation Operations function and is accountable for maintaining and strengthening the operational infrastructure, workflows, systems, controls, and team capacity required to support the Foundation’s long-term growth.

This is a hybrid position. Individuals in this position may work both at an approved off-site location and onsite at a primary location or multiple locations based on business needs

Responsibilities

Essential Functions:

Foundation Operations and Administration:- Lead the development, implementation, and ongoing improvement of Foundation operating procedures, workflows, calendars, controls, and administrative processes.- Translate approved Foundation strategies and leadership decisions into coordinated operational plans, timelines, responsibilities, and implementation requirements.- Exercise direct responsibility for operating procedures and workflows within the Foundation’s assigned operational scope.- Establish clear workflows, decision pathways, service expectations, and escalation processes among Foundation staff, Central Health departments, consultants, vendors, and external partners.- Identify operational barriers, dependencies, risks, resource needs, and process gaps and recommend practical solutions to the Foundation CEO.- Maintain current operational documentation, procedures, delegated authorities, reference materials, and service expectations.- Coordinate implementation of new or revised systems, policies, processes, controls, and operational practices.- Support consistent execution across Advancement, Strategy, Grants, Communications, Strategic Alignment and Impact, and Central Health partners.- Lead the Foundation’s operational response to emerging needs, implementation challenges, and cross-functional issues.- Lead and continuously strengthen the Foundation Operations function to support organizational needs and approved staffing plans.Financial Administration, Accounting Coordination, and Controls:- Lead the Foundation’s role in annual budgeting, forecasting, expense monitoring, financial reporting, and long-term operational planning in partnership with the Foundation CEO and Central Health Finance.- Serve as the Foundation’s primary operational lead for financial workflows, reporting requirements, issue resolution, and coordination with Central Health Finance.- Direct Foundation processes related to pledge accounting, fund accounting, grant accounting, restricted and unrestricted funds, gift administration, and related financial documentation.- Establish and maintain operational controls for Foundation revenue, expenditures, purchasing, contracts, gifts, grants, delegated approvals, and financial reporting.- Coordinate accurate and timely reconciliation of gifts, pledges, grants, funds, donor records, and financial information.- Maintain processes that support compliance with donor intent, gift restrictions, grant agreements, fund requirements, and stewardship obligations.- Partner with Finance, Legal, Grants, Advancement, and program leaders to support accurate establishment, administration, and reporting of restricted and unrestricted funds.- Coordinate supporting documentation for audits, tax filings, financial reviews, regulatory reporting, and corrective-action activities.- Identify, investigate, and escalate material financial, reconciliation, control, accounting, or fund-administration concerns.- Support implementation and administration of approved gift-acceptance, spending, investment, procurement, and financial-control policies.- Monitor operational and financial processes and recommend improvements to strengthen accuracy, accountability, efficiency, and sustainability.Gift, Donor, and Grant Administration:- Own the Foundation’s operational processes for gift processing, donor-record administration, acknowledgments, documentation, reconciliation, and reporting. - Establish and maintain consistent standards for donor records, gift documentation, restricted funds, pledge tracking, and stewardship-related information. - Coordinate closely with Advancement, Grants, Finance, Legal, and program leaders to ensure donor and funder commitments are accurately documented and administered. - Lead monitoring and tracking processes for grants, restricted funds, agreements, reporting requirements, and compliance obligations. - Partner closely with the Director of Foundation Grants Strategy on integrated grant workflows, monitoring, reporting, and issue resolution. - Maintain appropriate documentation and controls for gifts, grants, donor restrictions, fund agreements, and reporting commitments. - Identify and resolve gaps, inconsistencies, or risks in donor, gift, grant, and fund administration. - Ensure operational practices support donor trust, financial integrity, and compliance with organizational requirements.Governance, Compliance, and Records:- Lead the administrative operations supporting the Foundation Board and its committees.- Maintain Board and committee calendars, meeting schedules, agendas, materials, action logs, minutes, resolutions, approvals, and follow-up documentation.- Partner with the Foundation CEO, Board leadership, Legal, and appropriate staff to ensure meeting materials and governance records are complete, accurate, and timely.- Maintain Board rosters, terms, attendance, orientation materials, disclosures, policies, charters, and related records.- Coordinate Foundation compliance activities with Central Health Legal, Compliance, Finance, Internal Audit, Information Security, and other subject-matter experts.- Maintain an inventory and review schedule for Foundation policies, procedures, agreements, delegated authorities, required filings, and governance documents.- Support audits, monitoring reviews, compliance activities, and corrective-action plans and track operational follow-up.- Ensure Foundation records are organized, retained, secured, and accessible in accordance with applicable requirements.- Maintain administrative governance support while preserving the Foundation CEO’s responsibility for Board strategy, relationships, and executive accountability.CRM, Systems, Data, and Reporting:- Serve as the business owner for the Foundation CRM and donor-management systems.- Establish priorities, workflows, access controls, documentation, data standards, reporting requirements, integrations, and system-governance expectations.- Lead Foundation CRM implementation, configuration, testing, training, vendor management, upgrades, security coordination, and issue resolution.- Ensure donor, gift, grant, fund, financial, and operational information is accurate, timely, secure, and appropriately accessible.- Coordinate donor, financial, grant, reporting, and collaboration systems with Foundation functional leaders and Central Health Information Technology, as applicable.- Establish and maintain data-quality expectations, standard operating procedures, access controls, and reporting practices.- Develop and maintain operational dashboards, reporting tools, and performance measures.- Ensure Foundation-owned systems and records are appropriately maintained separately from Central Health systems where required.- Evaluate technology needs and recommend systems, enhancements, integrations, or vendor support necessary for Foundation operations.Shared Services, Contracts, and Procurement:- Serve as the primary operational liaison between the Foundation and Central Health shared-service departments. - Coordinate Foundation interactions with Finance, Human Resources, Payroll, Legal, Compliance, Information Technology, Procurement, Internal Audit, Communications, Facilities, and other departments. - Clarify and document service responsibilities, approval pathways, escalation processes, service expectations, contacts, and deliverables. - Monitor the effectiveness of shared-service arrangements and recommend improvements when gaps, duplication, delays, or accountability concerns are identified. - Coordinate Foundation contracts, vendors, consultants, procurement activities, and delegated approvals through Central Health processes, except where Foundation-specific arrangements are approved. - Directly manage Foundation-specific vendor and system relationships, including the Foundation CRM and related donor-management infrastructure. - Maintain appropriate documentation for contracts, procurement actions, vendor performance, service expectations, and delegated authority. - Escalate significant service, contract, procurement, compliance, or operational issues to the Foundation CEO.Operational Performance and Project Leadership:- Establish and monitor operational metrics, service standards, dashboards, reporting processes, and performance expectations.- Evaluate the timeliness, accuracy, consistency, efficiency, compliance, and effectiveness of Foundation operations.- Lead complex cross-functional operational projects, system implementations, and process-improvement initiatives.- Establish project objectives, timelines, roles, decision rights, dependencies, risks, and accountability.- Coordinate assigned vendors, consultants, contracts, and temporary resources within delegated authority.- Prepare operational updates, issue summaries, financial and performance information, and recommendations for the Foundation CEO, Foundation Board, and other appropriate audiences.- Facilitate resolution of cross-functional operational issues and escalate significant concerns when necessary.- Promote consistent documentation, accountability, continuous improvement, and effective use of Foundation resources.- Evaluate future operational staffing, technology, vendor, and resource needs and recommend investments necessary to support Foundation growth.Team Leadership and Development:- Recruit, develop, coach, and evaluate assigned employees within the Foundation Operations function.- Establish clear roles, performance expectations, priorities, and accountability for employees and other assigned resources. - Promote collaboration, professional development, cross-training, and operational continuity. - Ensure staff understand Foundation requirements, Central Health processes, donor and financial controls, governance expectations, and shared-service relationships. - Evaluate organizational capacity and recommend staffing, role, and structure changes as Foundation responsibilities expand. - Lead employees, consultants, vendors, and temporary resources in a manner consistent with organizational policies and delegated authority.

Qualifications

Education:

Bachelor's Degree (higher degree accepted) in public policy, public health, business, nonprofit management, healthcare administration, finance, accounting, or a related field. - Required

Master's Degree (higher degree accepted) in public policy, public health, business, nonprofit management, healthcare administration, finance, accounting, or a related field. - Preferred

Work Experience:

8 years of progressively responsible experience in foundation operations, advancement operations, nonprofit administration, healthcare administration, finance, accounting, business operations, grants administration, or a related field. - Required

5 years Experience leading complex operational functions involving finance, accounting coordination, controls, systems, data, compliance, governance, gift administration, grant administration, or shared services. - Required

5 years Experience developing and improving policies, procedures, workflows, controls, systems, and operational reporting. - Required

5 years Experience partnering with executive leaders and cross-functional departments such as Finance, Legal, Compliance, Human Resources, Information Technology, Procurement, and Internal Audit. - Required

Experience managing complex projects, vendors, contracts, systems, budgets, or organizational resources. - Required

Experience using operational and financial information to identify risks, resolve issues, and improve processes. - Required

Experience leading employees, consultants, vendors, project teams, or other resources and establishing clear goals and accountability. - Required

Experience within a healthcare foundation, health system, public-health organization, public hospital district, or similarly complex nonprofit organization. - Preferred

Experience with gift processing, restricted funds, pledge accounting, fund accounting, donor databases, grants administration, or fundraising operations. - Preferred

Experience serving as a business owner for a donor CRM or comparable enterprise system. - Preferred

Experience coordinating shared services between an affiliated foundation and a parent or supported organization. - Preferred

Experience supporting a governing Board or Board committee. - Preferred

Experience coordinating audits, compliance reviews, financial reviews, or corrective-action activities. - Preferred

Knowledge of Central Health systems, policies, departments, and operating processes. - Preferred

Travel Requirements:

Estimated Amout 10%. Regular local travel may be required for Central Health meetings, Board and committee activities, vendor meetings, operational coordination, and Foundation events. Occasional regional travel and periodic evening or weekend commitments may be required.

title: PPC Specialist | Solvy
description:
Hi!

We are Boosta, a holding tech company that creates, develops, and invests in digital businesses with global potential. Today, we collaborate with over 800 specialists from different parts of the world, and millions of users use our products and services.

We are currently looking for a PPC Specialist to join the Solvy business, which is developing a full-cycle online platform for working with legal, financial, and personal documents.

Solvy is now at a stage of active growth and scaling:

  • the team is growing;
  • the product is scaling without compromising stability or quality;
  • results are increasing 2–3x month over month.

In the role of PPC Specialist, you will:

  • Own the PPC channel for Solvy end-to-end: strategy, launch, optimization and scaling of campaigns.
  • Manage and allocate the paid budget to hit target CAC / ROAS / payback and grow revenue profitably.
  • Understand and model product economics (LTV, CAC, funnel conversion, retention) and use it to set bids, targets and budget decisions.
  • Set up and maintain correct tracking, conversions and value-based optimization together with analytics/dev.
  • Run a continuous testing roadmap: ads, keywords, audiences, bidding strategies, landing pages.
  • Find new growth points: new GEOs, campaign types, channels and funnel improvements together with product.
  • Build reporting and regularly present results, insights and plans to management.
  • Keep up with platform updates and market changes and turn them into competitive advantages.

We are looking for a candidate who:

  • 2+ years hands-on in PPC / paid search, with full ownership of accounts and budgets (Google Ads is a must; Microsoft Ads is a plus).
  • Proven track record of scaling paid acquisition profitably, with numbers to show for it (spend, ROAS/ROI, CAC, payback).
  • Strong grasp of product unit economics: LTV, CAC, payback period, conversion funnel, retention, margin; can build and defend a model in a spreadsheet.
  • Deep knowledge of bidding strategies (tCPA/tROAS, value-based bidding), campaign structures, Performance Max, keyword research and negative management.
  • Tracking & attribution: GA4, Google Tag Manager, conversion tracking, offline/server-side conversions, value-based conversion setup.
  • Confident with data: advanced Google Sheets/Excel, comfortable working with BI dashboards and raw data; basic SQL is a strong plus.
  • Systematic A/B testing of ads, landing pages and bidding approaches with clear hypotheses and conclusions.

Nice to have:

  • Experience in subscription / SaaS / EdTech or other products with LTV-based economics.
  • SQL, Looker Studio or another BI tool for self-serve analysis.
  • Experience with scripts and automation (Google Ads Scripts, API, rules).
  • Experience with other paid channels (Meta, TikTok, Apple Search Ads) and cross-channel budget allocation.
  • CRO experience: working with landing pages, funnels and product team on conversion growth.
  • Experience launching new GEOs and markets.
  • Ambition and readiness to grow into a Head of PPC role.

Our hiring flow:

  • Step 1: Pre-screen.
  • Step 2: Technical Interview.
  • Step 3: Test task.
  • Step 4: Job Offer.

Why Solvy? We offer:

Self-realization and growth:

  • Build a product from scratch and influence key decisions.
  • Grow together with the business at a fast pace.
  • Work in an environment with space and freedom to act.
  • Become part of a strong team of A-players who are ready to share expertise and boost each other.
  • Use learning opportunities: internal and external lectures, a large corporate library, compensation for external courses, English lessons, and speaking clubs.

Comfortable working conditions:

  • Work remotely or visit the office in Kyiv, coworking spaces in Lviv or Warsaw.
  • Plan your working day independently — we offer a flexible schedule, because results matter most.
  • Recharge and rest: 28 working days of paid vacation per year, up to 30 days of sick leave, and all public holidays fully covered.
  • Optionally arrange a transfer — swap a working day with a day off and vice versa.

Care and support:

  • Take care of your health: we provide medical insurance, a Mental Health program, and compensation for sessions with a psychologist.
  • Join socially meaningful initiatives, including the Ukrainian Victory Support program.
  • Celebrate important moments with us — receive gifts for special occasions in your life and career.
  • Participate in quarterly team buildings — online or offline — to make teamwork easy and enjoyable.

Join the project at a stage where you can truly influence, build, and grow together with the business!

title: Senior Medical Science Liaison
description:
Aroa Biosurgery Limited is a soft-tissue regeneration company that develops, manufactures, and distributes surgical products to improve healing in complex soft tissue reconstruction procedures. Founded in 2008, the company is built on proprietary AROA ECM™ Technology, a novel extracellular matrix biomaterial derived from ovine forestomach. Aroa’s mission is to “unlock regenerative healing for everybody” by delivering a next generation platform that significantly improve outcomes for patients, surgeons, and clinicians. The company focuses on making its solutions widely accessible and affordable, aiming to change the standard of care in tissue regeneration. Grounded in its name, which is Māori for “understanding,” Aroa integrates biological insight, structural design, and human factors to harness the body’s intrinsic ability to heal.

About the role:

As a Senior Medical Science Liaison, you will expand awareness and adoption of AROA’s technologies by serving as a scientific and clinical expert across evidence generation, education, KOL engagement, and field medical excellence. You will mentor field medical colleagues, support cross-functional initiatives, and strengthen AROA’s clinical and scientific presence globally.

Ideal candidate will be located in: Alaska, Arizona, California, Colorado, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Oregon, Texas, Utah, Washington or Wyoming

What you’ll do:

Drive Clinical Evidence Generation

  • Lead clinical evidence initiatives, including registries, case series, publications, conference presentations, and research activities.
  • Partner with Clinical Development to support study design and investigator-initiated research, ensuring projects stay on time and in scope.
  • Ensure compliance with ISO 14155 and applicable regulations in markets where AROA products are sold.
  • Collaborate with leadership, Marketing, Sales, and Clinical teams to build evidence that supports adoption and patient outcomes.

Educate and Empower

  • Translate complex clinical data into compelling educational content and presentations.
  • Deliver scientific, technical, and clinical training to internal teams and healthcare professionals.
  • Support clinicians across multiple specialties.
  • Provide clinical expertise and sales support during key customer engagements.
  • Influence organizational strategy related to education, training, clinical initiatives, marketing, and commercial growth.

Build Strategic Clinical Relationships

  • Lead conference planning and scientific engagement activities, including abstract submissions and KOL interactions.
  • Develop and strengthen relationships with leading clinicians, researchers, and scientific influencers.
  • Create and execute strategies to deepen engagement with key opinion leaders.
  • Serve as a trusted partner and scientific resource to customers and external stakeholders.

Serve as a Clinical Subject Matter Expert

  • Organize advisory boards and communicate actionable medical insights to internal stakeholders.
  • Provide expert clinical perspectives while advocating for patient-centric decision making.

What You'll Bring:

  • Bachelor's degree in Science, Medical Science or related healthcare discipline. MD or PhD preferred.
  • Valid driver's license and US Passport and ability to travel extensively.
  • Prior experience as a Medical Science Liaison.
  • 2-3 years of clinical experience within wound care, surgery, trauma, plastics, reconstructive surgery, or related specialties. 5+ years preferred
  • Experience participating in clinical research or evidence-generation activities.
  • Exceptional presentation, communication, and relationship-building skills.

We offer:

  • Comprehensive health benefits, including medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Competitive commission plans, enabling you to drive your own success
  • Generous paid time off, including your birthday off
  • 401(k) plan with company matching
  • A collaborative and inclusive culture that values diverse perspectives
  • A chance to directly influence patient outcomes while helping shape the future of wound care and soft tissue repair

Most importantly, you'll join a mission-led organization where your work matters. You'll build a territory, drive meaningful growth, and help bring life-changing healing solutions to more patients and providers around the world.

title: Sektionschef til Sekretariat og Sundhedspolitik – vær med tæt på de beslutninger, der former sundhedsvæsenet
description:
Vil du være en del af et stærkt ledelsesteam tæt på de beslutninger, der former sundhedsvæsenet – og være med til at sætte retning for politisk betjening, ledelsesbetjening og sekretariatsarbejdet i Danmarks største region?

Vi søger en sektionschef til Sekretariat og Sundhedspolitik i Koncern Sundhed, der kan sætte retning, skabe fremdrift og få mennesker og opgaver til at spille sammen i en hverdag tæt på den politiske og administrative topledelse i Region Østdanmark. Du skal trives med komplekse dagsordener, højt tempo og skiftende prioriteringer – og samtidig være en tydelig og nærværende leder for medarbejderne.

Ved årsskiftet bliver Region Hovedstaden og Region Sjælland til Region Østdanmark. Det betyder, at nye organisationer, samarbejder og arbejdsgange skal skabes på tværs – og at vi får mulighed for at tænke funktioner og løsninger på nye måder. Sekretariat og Sundhedspolitik får en central rolle i at få den nye organisation til at fungere og i at understøtte de politiske og ledelsesmæssige beslutninger, der skal forme fremtidens sundhedsvæsen.

En central ledelsesopgave

Som sektionschef bliver du en del af ledelsen i Sekretariat og Sundhedspolitik og får sammen med den nuværende enhedschef og sektionschef ansvar for at drive enheden.

Du får en central rolle i at understøtte enheden i at sikre en god understøttelse af vores politikere og ledelse og drive tværgående processer og skabe sammenhæng i komplekse dagsordener på sundhedsområdet. I Sekretariat og Sundhedspolitik har vi bl.a. ansvaret for betjeningen af sundhedsrådene og de politiske udvalg på sundhedsområdet, understøtter ledelsen og enhederne i centeret og driver omstillingen mod nye digitale arbejdsgange og løser opgaver med medarbejderinddragelse og arbejdsmiljø.

Du skal både kunne løfte blikket og forstå den konkrete opgave. Det betyder, at du skal kunne se den politiske og strategiske retning, understøtte kvaliteten i leverancerne og samtidig skabe rammerne for, at medarbejderne kan lykkes i en hverdag, hvor dagsordener og deadlines ofte flytter sig hurtigt.

Dine opgaver

Som sektionschef kan du blandt andet få ansvar for at:

  • være med til, sammen med det øvrige ledelsesteam, at lede og udvikle enheden fagligt, organisatorisk og personalemæssigt med fokus på trivsel, kvalitet og resultater
  • sikre høj kvalitet og fremdrift i den politiske betjening og ledelsesbetjeningen
  • prioritere og koordinere opgaver i en hverdag med mange samtidige leverancer og korte deadlines
  • understøtte udarbejdelsen af beslutningsoplæg, politiske sager, notater, taler, præsentationer og øvrigt materiale til politikere og ledelse
  • drive og understøtte større tværgående processer og dagsordener på tværs af Koncern Sundhed og Region Østdanmark
  • skabe gode samarbejdsrelationer til Koncern Sundheds øvrige enheder, hospitalerne og den øvrige regionale administration
  • udvikle arbejdsgange og samarbejdsformer, så vi arbejder effektivt, koordineret og med høj kvalitet

Du får et tæt ledelsesmæssigt samspil med enhedens enhedschef og nuværende sektionschef. I ledergruppen har vi et fælles ansvar for helheden og for at skabe sammenhæng på tværs af sektioner, fagligheder og geografier.

Du bliver en del af Koncern Sundheds ledelse, som består af direktionen, 13 enhedschefer og 18 sektionschefer. Du refererer til enhedschefen Sekretariat og Sundhedspolitik Lise Graae.

Ledelse i Koncern Sundhed

Som leder i Koncern Sundhed forventer vi, at du:

  • kan udøve strategisk ledelse og omsætte mål og ambitioner til handling
  • er en kvalificeret sparringspartner for det politiske niveau, koncerndirektionen og direktionen
  • bidrager aktivt til den samlede ledelsesgruppe og tager medansvar for helheden på tværs
  • kan navigere sikkert blandt mange interessenter og samarbejdspartnere både i og uden for regionen
  • er nysgerrig på den virkelighed, der kendetegner fx hospitalerne og de øvrige enheder i regionerne
  • skaber tillid, retning og engagement gennem en tydelig, relationel og ordentlig ledelsesstil.

Din profil

Vi forestiller os, at du:

  • har en relevant videregående uddannelse inden for samfundsvidenskab eller lignende
  • har erfaring med en politisk styret organisation og ledelsesbetjening
  • kan navigere sikkert i komplekse organisationer med mange interessenter og forskellige hensyn
  • kan skabe overblik og prioritere, når mange vigtige opgaver lander samtidig
  • er stærk både analytisk og kan gøre komplekse problemstillinger klare og beslutningsparate
  • kan drive processer og skabe fremdrift på tværs af fagligheder og organisatoriske grænser
  • motiveres af at udvikle både medarbejdere, opgaveløsning og organisation.

Du behøver ikke kende alle dele af sundhedsvæsenet på forhånd. Det er heller ikke krav at du har meget lang ledelseserfaring. Det afgørende er, at du har den politiske og organisatoriske forståelse, gennemslagskraften og personligheden til at sætte retning, skabe følgeskab og få ting til at ske – også i en kompleks organisation med mange interessenter.

Med til at bygge noget nyt

Med etableringen af Region Østdanmark den 1. januar 2027 bliver du en del af Danmarks største region med omkring 2,8 mio. borgere og mere end 65.000 medarbejdere.

Sammenlægningen er samtidig en historisk stor organisatorisk forandring. Nye strukturer og samarbejder skal etableres, sundhedsreformen skal omsættes til praksis, og politiske ambitioner skal blive til konkrete løsninger.

Sekretariat og Sundhedspolitik står centralt i den udvikling. Vi er tæt på de beslutninger, der former sundhedsvæsenet, og vores opgave er både at sikre stærk politisk og administrativ betjening og at skabe sammenhæng og fremdrift på tværs af organisationen.

Pr. 1. januar 2027 vil Sekretariat og Sundhedspolitik bestå af godt 45 medarbejdere med base i Hillerød og Sorø. Du kan forvente at få fast base ét af stederne – afhængighed af dine præferencer og, hvilke faglige områder og opgaver, du får det primære ansvar for.

Du skal dog være indstillet på, at der løbende vil være møder og opgaver ude i regionen – selvom vi i hverdagen klarer mange ting på teams, mails og telefon.

Vi er i ledelsen i gang med at lægge alle sporene, og vi har brug for én som har mod og lyst til at træde til og sammen med os og medarbejderne bidrage til at forme, hvordan vi fremover arbejder med politisk betjening, ledelsesbetjening og tværgående koordinering i det nye Koncern Sundhed. Sammen med dig aftaler vi, hvilke faglige områder og opgaver du får det primære ledelsesansvar for, så vi bedst muligt bringer dine erfaringer og styrker i spil. Vi kan samtidig aftale, hvor du foretrækker at arbejde fra.

Det praktiske

Er du interesseret, så send os en motiveret ansøgning, CV og eksamenspapirer senest 28. oktober 2026.

Stillingen er en fuldtidsstilling med tiltrædelse 1. januar 2027.

Vi holder 1. samtale den 2 og 3. november 2026 og 2. samtale den 16. november 2026. Der kan indgå test mellem 1. og 2. samtale.

Som sektionschef ansættes du iht. aftale for chefer, med indplacering som øvrige administrative chefer på trin 49 + tillæg. Der vil være mulighed for at forhandle individuelle tillæg afhængigt af stillingen samt din erfaring og dine kvalifikationer.

Vil du vide mere?

Har du spørgsmål, kan du kontakte enhedschef Lise Graae på mobil 21 77 60 88.

title: Sterile Processing Technician (SPT)
description:

Working hours are five days per week, eight hours per day. Shifts are assigned based on facility need: 7:00 AM to 3:30 PM, 3:00 PM to 11:30 PM, or 11:00 PM to 7:30 AM.

  • Reassembling and packaging instruments per AAMI, AORN, FDA, OSHA, and manufacturer instructions.

Qualifications

    • Certification as a Certified Registered Central Service Technician (CRCST) or higher by International Association of Healthcare Central Service Material Management (IAHCSMM/HSPA).
    • Graduation from a nationally recognized CRCST training program with a minimum of 2 current years of documented work in the field.
    • Graduation from a nationally recognized Operating Room Technician training program with a minimum of 2 current years of documented work experience in a Sterile Processing Service environment.

Location

  • Fresno VA Medical Center located at 2615 East Clinton Avenue, Fresno, CA 93703
  • This is a full-time onsite position
Shift
  • Working hours are five days per week, eight hours per day
  • Shifts are assigned based on facility need: 7:00 AM to 3:30 PM, 3:00 PM to 11:30 PM, or 11:00 PM to 7:30 AM

title: Research Associate

  • Supporting a Senior Analyst in preparing and publishing a wide range of research reports

title: Archivist (NPS, Aztec Ruins National Monument)
description:
The Cultural Resource Services Program (CRS) at the Great Basin Institute (GBI), in cooperation with Aztec Ruins National Monument (AZRU), is hiring one Project Archivist to work cooperatively under the direction of the National Park Service (NPS) Archivist for Chaco Culture National Historical Park and Aztec Ruins National Monument, to support the Parks’ combined Museum & Archives Program. The role of the Archivist is to complete appraisal, arrangement, rehousing and cataloging of approximately 21 linear feet of NPS field documentation pertaining to archeological stabilization and preservation work at AZRU dating back to 1956. Approximately seven linear feet of inadequately processed preservation documentation will be processed and integrated with 15 linear feet of unprocessed documentation from 1998-2018, according to professional archival standards, cataloged into the Museum Collections Management System (MCMS), and a finding aid created. Vulnerable color images will be digitized and metadata created following FADGI guidelines and materials packaged for cold storage. Born-digital records will be retrieved from obsolete storage media and moved to managed server storage for long-term preservation.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Perform collections appraisal based on NPS and DOI records schedules and archival appraisal criteria
  • Arrange, describe and rehouse records according to professional standards.
  • Produce a 508 compliant PDF finding aid and entry in ArchivesSpace (New Mexico Archives Online) for access and discoverability.
  • Digitize photographic materials for preservation and access.

Timeline:

  • Position intended to begin in late November or early December 2026; 21 weeks.
  • Full time (40 hours/week);
  • Schedule: 5 days/week, 8 hours/day

Location:

The position will be located at the NPS CHCU-AZRU Museum & Archives Program repository located on the University of New Mexico (UNM) campus in Albuquerque, NM. At least one day trip to AZRU by vehicle of up to 12 hours will be required.

title: Workday Student Advising and Curriculum Management Consultant
description:
Join Cognizant's Workday Student Practice in Australia and New Zealand and help universities transform how they manage curriculum and support their students. Working directly with clients on Workday Student deployments, you'll lead design and configuration across curriculum management, academic planning and advising, and guide institutions on how the solution can best meet their needs and support their strategic goals. This is a real opportunity to grow your career while helping shape how the sector operates.

This role suits someone with a background in curriculum planning, academic administration or student advising who wants to apply that experience in a consulting career. You'll bring higher education and student systems expertise to every engagement, working closely with academic leaders, registrars and advisors, and making sure your designs align with Student Records and other areas of the Workday platform.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead discovery and design sessions for academic advising, academic planning, curriculum management and related student processes.
  • Configure the course catalogue, offerings and prerequisite rules, and support integration with the institution's curriculum management system.
  • Design advising models including advisor assignments, caseloads, student cohorts, notes, appointments and communications.
  • Configure academic requirements, student planning and progress monitoring in alignment with institutional policy and regulatory requirements.
  • Work with Student Records and academic stakeholders to align curriculum, enrolment, progression and completion outcomes.
  • Document requirements, design decisions and configuration
  • Apply your higher education experience to shape practical future-state processes for curriculum and advising teams
  • Bring an understanding of how Australian and New Zealand universities operate to design discussions, so Workday Student is configured for local academic structures, terminology and policy settings.
  • Identify data, security, reporting and integration requirements associated with advising and curriculum processes.
  • Prepare and execute unit testing, support end to end testing and assist with defect resolution.
  • Support data conversion validation, cutover preparation, training and go live readiness.
  • Provide clear advice on Workday leading practices while recognising institutional context and policy obligations.
  • Contribute reusable configuration guidance, test assets and delivery methods to the Cognizant Student Practice.

Experience we are looking for

  • Experience in academic administration, curriculum management, registrar services, academic advising, student success or a related higher education function in an Australian or New Zealand University.
  • Understanding of academic programs, courses, curriculum approval, progression, degree requirements and advising practices.
  • Familiarity with the regulatory context for curriculum and student progression in Australia or New Zealand, such as the Higher Education Standards Framework, AQF, ESOS National Code and HESA Support for Students requirements, or CUAP programme approval and the Pastoral Care Code.
  • Proven experience guiding business stakeholders through key operational and policy decisions, including presenting options, explaining trade-offs and securing agreement.
  • Experience implementing, supporting or serving as a super-user for student information systems (SIS).
  • Ability to translate academic policy and operational requirements into structured system design.
  • Experience facilitating workshops, documenting decisions and working across academic and professional teams preferred.
  • Experience with testing, data validation, training or deployment readiness activities preferred.

About the Cognizant Workday Student Practice

The Cognizant Workday Student Practice is focused exclusively on helping universities across Australia and New Zealand transform the way they support students, faculty and administrators throughout the student lifecycle.

What makes our practice different is the combination of higher education practitioners and Workday specialists working together. Many of our consultants have worked inside universities as academic services professionals before moving into consulting. That experience allows us to bring practical insight into the operational, regulatory and policy considerations that shape solution design.

We work with institutions to design and implement sustainable Workday Student solutions that support local regulatory requirements, align to institutional strategy and remain adaptable as university needs evolve. Our goal is not simply to deploy technology, but to help universities establish a foundation they can continue to own, operate and enhance long after implementation is complete.

title: Project Manager - Touring N.A.

title: Quality Control Auditor - 1st Shift
description:
Quality Control Auditor

Position Overview

The Quality Control Auditor performs inspection and testing activities to ensure quality of materials and products used or produced by Quaker Windows and Doors. This is an entry level position that will inspect materials, monitor build processes and document quality results . At the direction of the Quality Assurance Supervisor, the position will communicate and coordinate quality control objectives with production operations to maximize product reliability and minimize costs. The Quality Control Auditor I examines completed and in-process products for quality and conformance to established specifications and standards.

Division: Commercial

Job Type: Full-Time

FLSA: Non-Exempt

Shift: 1st (Day Shift), Mon-Friday, 6am - 2:30pm

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Learn to perform quality review on products in process of being made for one product line
  • Learn to perform quality control audits on finished products
  • Confer with manufacturing departments personnel to coordinate quality activities
  • Learn to use various inspection tools such as a calipers, angle gage, paint thickness gage, or thermal fill hardness tester to evaluate parts
  • Learn to document audit activities using a tablet with quality reporting software to document audit activities. Note the Pass/Fail results. Then for audit fails document the issue with pictures and assign the rework or repair to a Team Lead
  • Support production leaders and operators for interpretation and methods following set standards
  • Learn to interpret and support quality policies and work instructions to ensure compliance with quality standards and documents
  • Work with a mentor to analyze and resolve build problems or assist workers in solving build problems
  • Assist in the development of inspection and audit reports to document audit performance and improvement opportunities
  • Assist in developing new methods to resolve problems occurring during quality assurance activities
  • Fill in at different workstations as auditing needs require
  • Prompt and regular attendance at an assigned work location.
  • Interact and communicate with employees in an appropriate manner.
  • Availability on site to confer with staff members with whom the employee must interact on a regular basis.
  • Review and analyze priority lists of audits that need performed.
  • Plan, prioritize and monitor build activities, such as but not limited to developmental builds, mocks up units and sample units.
  • Complete assigned tasks/projects in a timely manner, including tasks or activities as assigned by the Quality Supervisor or Manager.

No direct management or supervisory responsibilities.

Safety

Observe safety and security policies and procedures, including proper use of Personal Protective Equipment including but not limited to eye and toe protection. Steal or composite toed footwear required. Employees must report potentially unsafe conditions and use equipment and materials properly. Employees must follow department-specific safety requirements such as Safe Lift and Safe Product Handling Guidelines.

Travel

Qualifications

An individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.

  • Familiarity with Microsoft Office software: Excel, Word, Outlook
  • Basic mechanical comprehension of windows and doors

  • Safe and efficient usage of power tools such as saw, etc.
  • Expanding knowledge in the technical build
  • Proficient in fraction and decimal units of measurement

Preferred Education and Experience

The expectation is that the individual has achieved a minimum level of education and/or related expertise to qualify for this position.

  • High School Diploma or a Passed General Education Development Test Preferred
  • Minimum 90 Days Experience in Manufacturing

Competencies and Skills

  • Quality Focused
  • Problem Solving
  • Accuracy
  • Communication Proficiency & Listening
  • Leadership Abilities / Supportive Leadership
  • Personal Effectiveness / Credibility
  • Basic Mathematical Skills
  • Reliability
  • Thoroughness
  • Time Management

Position Type and Expected Hours of Work

This is a full-time position. Days and hours of work are Friday through Sunday 6:00am to 6:30pm.

Physical Demands

The demands and environment characteristics described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

This is a manufacturing job. The employee must be able to:

  • regularly lift and/or carry objects weighing up to 50 pounds, and occasionally lift and/or move up to 100 pounds through team lift;
  • work shifts of at least 8-10 hours, and occasionally longer, for 5-6 days each week;
  • stand for prolonged periods; and
  • occasionally push, pull, stoop, bend, climb or balance; and kneel, crouch or crawl as necessary.

Vision abilities required by this job may include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

If an assisted lift is available, the position must use the assisted lift or use team lift any time objects exceeding 75 pounds need lifting or carrying.

It is an essential job function and safety rule, applicable to every employee working in a safety sensitive classified position, to be able to work in a constant state of alertness and in a safe manner.

Various different types of Personal Protective Equipment might be required based on the employee's work location. The noise level in the work environment may require hearing protection.

title: Customs Compliance Specialist
description:

Humanscale is the premier designer and manufacturer of ergonomic products that improve health and comfort at work. We have a focus on sustainability with over 70% of our products currently certified as having a Net Positive impact on the environment. Our award-winning office products – seating, sit/stand desks, technology support and lighting – have led the industry in performance and simplicity for over 40 years.

Overview

The Customs Compliance Specialist will be responsible for supporting and maintaining customs and international trade compliance across the Company’s North America operation. This role ensures compliance with applicable import and export regulations, customs requirements and supply chain security programs including CTPAT. Key responsibilities include customs documentation and entry review, validating HTS classification and origin data, trade agreement compliance, and execution of related processes/procedures that ensure Humanscale complies with all customs regulations while exercising the highest standard of reasonable care. This is a fast-paced, high-volume environment.

Responsibilities

  • Coordinate with customs broker to resolve questions and provide information at the time of port arrival, including, but not limited to: HTS, FTA eligibility, valuation verification, Tariff assessments, and AD/CVD applicability.
  • Perform daily audits of Customs Entries.
  • Compile specific documentation for the purpose of drawback claims.
  • Create weekly reports on product movement through US, Canadian and Mexican borders.
  • Create recurring reports on US, Canadian and Mexican Customs spend.
  • Contribute ideas and suggestions to improve processes.
  • Maintain department records/files as required.
  • Support the CTPAT committee’s initiatives to ensure continued compliance.
  • Provide Planners and Management with applicable HTS and corresponding duty rates prior to import.
  • Support and assist with any departmental need in or outside the company, i.e., Customs, broker, planners, management, etc.
  • Additional duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree preferred; Associate’s degree required.
  • 1-3 years of experience required in data analysis and Customs related functions.
  • Knowledge and understanding of U.S. Customs import, as well as Canadian and Mexican customs processes.
  • Attention to detail with precision in reporting.
  • Excellent verbal, written, and communication skills.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
  • Excellent organizational, analytical, and interpersonal skills with the ability to disseminate significant amounts of information.
  • Ability to exercise independent judgment.
  • Ability to prioritize workload and multitask.
  • Strong problem-solving skills including root cause identification.

  • Ability to balance team and individual responsibilities; provides and welcomes feedback

Description

Project 137 is Quantum Sky’s IP and solution engine. It is organized around four practices: Quantum, Digital Platforms, Decision Advantage, and Cyber. We are looking for Project 137’s Chief Engineer, the person who turns what those practices devise into software that runs, and who answers for how well it is built. You will build modern, cloud-native microservice applications for the U.S. government: the Department of War (DoD/DoW), the Intelligence Community, and federal civilian agencies. Increasingly, the services you build will be agents, and the applications they compose will be agentic workflows that do real work alongside the people they serve.

You will also change how we build. That means running an agentic SDLC: agents that help design, write, test, secure, review, and ship code, under the discipline that federal delivery demands. We intend to deliver faster than our competitors, with fewer defects and better evidence for accreditation, and to be able to prove it.

This role sits where next-generation engineering meets proven delivery. Quantum Sky already builds and operates mission systems for DoD and federal customers. Your job is to set the engineering standard that Project 137 and our programs build on: software that is secure, scalable, compliant, and accessible by design rather than by remediation. You will also show customers what modern software delivery looks like inside a federal boundary. This isn’t a “PowerPoint architect” role, and it isn’t a heads-down coding role either.

Responsibilities:

  • Architect. Set the target architecture for Project 137 applications: containerized microservices, event-driven integration, API-first design, and agentic services that plug into all of it cleanly. Design for the environments our customers actually run: government and classified cloud regions, on-premises enclaves, hybrid estates, and disconnected or bandwidth-constrained edge deployments. Cloud-native where it can be; cloud-portable where it must be.
  • Build. Lead Project 137’s software engineers to take solutions from concept to working capability that can be demonstrated, accredited, and deployed. Build agentic workflows that hold up in production: orchestration, tool use, memory, guardrails, evaluation, and observability, with humans in the loop where the mission requires it. No AI-washing: agents that do real work inside real mission workflows.
  • Engineer for Assurance. Own the quality of what we ship. Our products leave the building free of known exploitable vulnerabilities and stay that way, through secure design, continuous scanning, fast patching, and an honest vulnerability backlog. They are engineered to scale, with load, resilience, and cost tested before a customer finds the limits. They meet federal cyber, compliance, and accessibility requirements from the first commit: NIST and FedRAMP controls, DoD impact levels, and Section 508. Compliance is built into the pipeline, not bolted on before an ATO.
  • Use Open Source Intelligently. Build on open source where it makes us faster and better, and know exactly what we depend on. Govern it: approved components, license compliance, provenance, SBOMs, and a clear view of which projects are healthy and which are a liability. Contribute back where it serves the mission and our reputation.
  • Change the Way We Build. Stand up and run an agentic SDLC and DevSecOps pipeline: AI-assisted design, coding, testing, code review, and security scanning, wired into CI/CD with the controls, provenance, and evidence an authorizing official will ask for. Measure it. Velocity, quality, and cost to deliver should improve visibly, and you should be able to say by how much.
  • Strengthen the Whole Portfolio. Work closely with the Quantum, Digital Platforms, Decision Advantage, and Cyber practice leaders so that their offerings stand on a common engineering foundation: reusable services, shared platforms, and patterns that are not reinvented for each pursuit. Every practice ships software; make sure ours is a strength across the portfolio.
  • Build the Team. Recruit, develop, and keep engineers who are fluent in both modern software and agentic AI, and who can work in cleared environments. Set the bar for engineering craft and hold it. Decide where we build, where we buy, and where we partner.
  • Win. Drive the team to deliver demonstrations that are compelling, working, and true to what we can field. Coach the demo team on the story, the script, and the recovery when something fails live. Where the stakes call for it, step in and lead the technical demonstration yourself.

How You Will Lead:

  • The Builder-Leader. You still read code, and you can still write it. Engineers follow you because you understand their work, not because of your title.
  • Engineering Judgment. You know when a monolith is the right answer, when a microservice is a liability, and when an agent is the wrong tool. You make the trade-offs explicit and stand behind them.
  • Relationships Across the Business. You earn the trust of business unit leaders, program managers, and capture managers, the people who own the customers and the delivery. They bring you in early because you make their programs stronger and their pursuits more credible. You treat them as partners, not as internal customers to be managed.
  • Clarity Under Pressure. You can explain an architecture to a program executive, an authorizing official, and a junior developer, and each leaves knowing what matters to them. When a release is at risk, you say so early and plainly.
  • Fluency Across Generations of Technology. You are as credible discussing the systems agencies and commands run today as the platforms they are moving to, and you know how to get from one to the other without breaking the mission on the way. You can take a customer on that modernization journey and show where agentic AI earns its place in it.

Qualifications

Required:

  • The Blueprint: 15+ years of software engineering and engineering leadership, including 7+ years building and delivering software for the federal government (DoD/DoW, IC, or federal civilian).
  • The Architecture: Deep, hands-on experience designing and delivering cloud-native microservice applications: containers and Kubernetes, service mesh, event streaming, API management, and the data patterns that go with them, in AWS, Azure, or Google government environments. You have built systems that scaled under real load and can explain what broke along the way.
  • The Pipeline: A record of building and running DevSecOps pipelines in federal environments: CI/CD, infrastructure as code, automated testing, static and dynamic security testing, software composition analysis, SBOMs and software supply-chain security, and software factory or continuous ATO practices.
  • The Assurance Record: Evidence that you have shipped federal software that passed security assessment, held up in operation, and stayed patched, along with a working approach to open-source governance: license, provenance, and vulnerability management across a real dependency tree.
  • The AI Edge: Hands-on experience building LLM-based and agentic applications (orchestration frameworks, retrieval, tool calling, Model Context Protocol, evaluation, and guardrails), and using AI coding agents to accelerate the software lifecycle. You know where agents create leverage and where they create risk, and you can explain both to an authorizing official.
  • The Leadership Record: A track record of leading multiple engineering teams through delivery against federal contracts, schedules, and accreditation requirements, and of growing the engineers on them.
  • The Standards: Working fluency in NIST 800-53, RMF, FedRAMP and DoD Cloud Computing Security Requirements Guide impact levels, the NIST Secure Software Development Framework (SP 800-218), the DoD Zero Trust Reference Architecture, and Section 508 / WCAG accessibility, and in how each shapes the way software is designed and shipped.

Desired:

  • Mission Familiarity: Experience building for DoD/DoW or IC mission customers, including in classified environments.
  • The Edge: Experience delivering software to disconnected, intermittent, and limited-bandwidth (DDIL) and tactical edge environments.
  • Portfolio Ownership: Prior leadership of an engineering practice, software factory, or product line with accountability for reuse, cost, and growth.
  • A Public Voice: A recognized point of view on modern federal software delivery or agentic engineering, through talks, published work, open-source contributions, or industry working groups.

Clearance:

  • Active SECRET or higher (Top Secret/SCI preferred).

About Quantum Sky

Compensation:

  • Compensation is unique to each candidate and relative to the skills and experience they bring to the position. The salary range for this position is typically between $225,000-$265,000. This does not guarantee a specific salary as compensation is based upon multiple factors such as education, experience, certifications, and other requirements, and may fall outside of the above-stated range.

Benefits:

  • Highlights of our benefits include Health/Dental/Vision, 401(k) match, Paid Time Off, STD/LTD/Life Insurance, Referral Bonuses, professional development reimbursement, and parental leave.

The world the mission operates in is going post-quantum, contested, and machine-speed. Quantum Sky engineers the advantage across cyber, networks, software, and quantum because the mission demands dominance, not parity. We don't follow the map. We draw it.

At Quantum Sky, we believe that success starts with our people. We foster a collaborative, innovative, and mission-driven environment where every team member plays a critical role in shaping the future of technology. Are you ready to join #TeamQuantumSky?

Quantum Sky Engineering LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer; all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, [sexual orientation, gender identity,] national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any characteristic protected by applicable law.

None
