title: Senior Director, Pharmaceutical Writing Services
description:
Position Summary

Criterion Edge is seeking an experienced Senior Director to lead its Pharmaceutical Writing Services group, with substantial hands-on pharmaceutical and biologic regulatory medical writing expertise and the ability to independently author and lead complex medical device clinical evaluations as needed.
The Senior Director will provide scientific, technical, and operational leadership for pharmaceutical writing engagements, including oversight of complex clinical submission programs, client relationships, writer development, resourcing, and quality. The successful candidate must also be capable of independently leading end-to-end Clinical Evaluation Report (CER) projects under the EU MDR, including responses to Notified Body questions.
This is a hands-on writing leadership role, not solely a people-management, regulatory affairs, or review position. The Senior Director must be able to personally author and critically review complex pharmaceutical and medical device documents and serve as a technical authority for writers, project teams, and clients.

Required Pharmaceutical Writing Experience

Candidates must have:
  1. At least 8 years of direct pharmaceutical and/or biologic regulatory medical writing experience, with substantial recent hands-on authorship of complex clinical and regulatory submission documents.
  2. Demonstrated end-to-end leadership of pharmaceutical writing programs or major submission workstreams, including planning, authoring, review coordination, issue resolution, and delivery of submission-ready documents, rather than experience limited to discrete sections, editing, quality control, or project management.
  3. Demonstrated ability to develop and communicate pharmaceutical and biologic clinical regulatory writing strategies, coordinating across clinical, regulatory, biostatistics, safety, and other functions.
  4. Demonstrated ability to advise clients on pharmaceutical regulatory guidance, submission expectations, and implications for clinical and regulatory documents.
Relevant pharmaceutical and biologic regulatory writing experience may include:
  1. Regulatory submissions: INDs, NDAs, BLAs, and global regulatory dossiers.
  2. CTD clinical documentation: Clinical Overviews, Clinical Summaries, Integrated Summaries of Safety (ISS), and Integrated Summaries of Efficacy (ISE).
  3. Clinical development documents: Clinical Study Reports (CSRs), clinical study protocols, and Investigator's Brochures (IBs).
  4. Regulatory authority interactions: Regulatory briefing documents and responses to regulatory authority questions.
  5. Safety and benefit-risk documentation: Integrated safety evaluations, benefit-risk assessments, and related regulatory documentation.
  6. Regulatory strategy and advisory services: Development of regulatory writing strategies and advising clients on evolving regulatory requirements and submission expectations.
Experience planning and coordinating clinical submission documents across eCTD Modules 2 through 5, including integrated clinical summaries and major marketing application workstreams, is strongly preferred.
Candidates must demonstrate the ability to lead pharmaceutical writing engagements independently, including development of the writing strategy, coordination of cross-functional reviews, resolution of conflicting reviewer comments, and direct communication with sponsors and regulatory stakeholders.

Required Medical Device Experience

Candidates must have:
  1. At least 5 years of direct medical device regulatory or clinical writing experience, with substantial end-to-end EU MDR CER leadership experience.
  2. Demonstrated ability to independently scope, author, lead, and finalize regulator-ready CERs, including resolving complex clinical evidence issues and addressing Notified Body questions without day-to-day supervision. Experience limited to editing, quality control, review, project management, or authorship of individual CER sections is insufficient.
  3. Demonstrated ability to develop and communicate regulatory strategies for medical device programs.
  4. Demonstrated ability to guide clients on regulatory updates, changing requirements, and the potential impact of those changes on clinical and regulatory documentation.
Independent CER leadership must include the ability to direct and perform the following activities, as applicable:
  1. Clinical evaluation planning and strategy: Clinical Evaluation Plan (CEP) development, project scoping, and clinical evaluation strategy.
  2. Literature review and clinical evidence assessment: State-of-the-art development, systematic literature review strategy, literature screening, clinical data appraisal, and evidence synthesis.
  3. Clinical evaluation and benefit-risk assessment: Evaluation of device safety, performance, clinical benefits, equivalence (where applicable), and benefit-risk conclusions.
  4. PMS and PMCF integration: Evaluation and integration of post-market surveillance (PMS) and post-market clinical follow-up (PMCF) data into clinical evaluations.
  5. CER development and regulatory support: Authoring and finalization of regulator-ready CERs, lifecycle updates, and responses to Notified Body questions and deficiencies.
  6. Regulatory strategy and client advisory: Interpretation of evolving EU MDR, MEDDEV, MDCG, and related regulatory requirements and advising clients on their implications for clinical evaluation.
Candidates must demonstrate current working knowledge of EU MDR clinical evaluation requirements, MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev. 4, and applicable MDCG guidance.

Preferred U.S. Medical Device Submission Experience

Candidates should also have experience authoring, leading, or substantially contributing to U.S. medical device regulatory documentation; direct 510(k) authorship is preferred.
Relevant experience may include:
  1. FDA regulatory submissions: 510(k), De Novo, and Premarket Approval (PMA) submissions.
  2. Regulatory and scientific documentation: Predicate device comparisons, substantial equivalence assessments, clinical and performance evidence summaries, and supporting technical documentation.
  3. FDA interactions: Preparation of responses to FDA questions, requests for additional information, and regulatory deficiencies.
  4. Regulatory strategy and client advisory: Development of U.S. market access strategies and advising clients on evolving FDA requirements and submission expectations.
Leadership Responsibilities
The Senior Director will:
  1. Lead Criterion Edge’s Pharmaceutical Writing Services group, with accountability for technical quality, delivery, staff development, and the successful execution of pharmaceutical and biologic regulatory writing engagements.
  2. Establish consistent pharmaceutical writing processes, quality expectations, and technical review standards while maintaining direct authorship capacity for priority or high-complexity deliverables.
  3. Serve as the senior pharmaceutical regulatory medical writing expert for complex clinical submission programs, while providing independent technical leadership for CER projects when needed.
  4. Lead pharmaceutical client scoping discussions, proposal input, kickoffs, and ongoing senior-level client communications.
  5. Develop and communicate regulatory and medical writing strategies appropriate to each project.
  6. Guide clients on regulatory updates, changing requirements, emerging guidance, and their potential impact on regulatory strategy and documentation.
  7. Plan pharmaceutical writing deliverables, budgets, timelines, resource requirements, and cross-functional review cycles; oversee execution and address delivery risks.
  8. Independently author or lead pharmaceutical regulatory documents and major submission workstreams, and lead complex EU MDR CER projects from planning through finalization, including Notified Body deficiency responses.
  9. Review complex scientific and regulatory documents for scientific accuracy, regulatory compliance, consistency, and overall quality.
  10. Lead, mentor, and provide substantive scientific and regulatory oversight to Principal and Senior Medical Writers; assign work appropriate to writer expertise and provide actionable feedback.
  11. Provide technical direction when project teams encounter complex scientific, regulatory, or writing issues.
  12. Serve as an escalation point for high-risk or technically complex projects.
  13. Work directly with client regulatory, clinical, biostatistics, safety, quality, and medical teams.
  14. Lead client discussions involving regulatory strategy, document development, review resolution, regulatory updates, and submission readiness.
  15. Translate regulatory changes into clear, actionable recommendations for clients and internal project teams.
  16. Support development and improvement of writing procedures, templates, training materials, and quality standards.
  17. Support business development activities by providing technical expertise during proposals, capability discussions, and prospective client meetings.
  18. Own or actively support writer allocation, capacity planning, project estimates, and identification of appropriate resources for pharmaceutical and medical device engagements.
  19. Maintain awareness of evolving medical device and pharmaceutical regulatory requirements and communicate relevant changes to clients and internal teams.

Minimum Qualifications

Candidates must meet all of the following requirements:
  1. Bachelor's degree or higher in life sciences, medicine, pharmacy, biomedical sciences, engineering, or another relevant scientific discipline.
  2. 5+ years of medical device regulatory or clinical writing experience, including substantive CER authorship.
  3. 5+ years independently leading end-to-end CER projects, including substantial EU MDR CER work from 2019 to the present and direct experience resolving Notified Body questions.
  4. 8+ years of pharmaceutical or biologic regulatory medical writing experience, including substantial hands-on authorship and leadership of complex submission documents.
  5. Demonstrated end-to-end leadership of a significant pharmaceutical submission program or major clinical submission workstream, with personal authorship of major regulatory documents.
  6. Demonstrated experience working with eCTD-based pharmaceutical submissions.
  7. Experience substantially contributing to U.S. medical device regulatory submissions; direct 510(k) authorship is strongly preferred.
  8. Demonstrated experience developing regulatory strategies for medical device and/or pharmaceutical programs.
  9. Demonstrated ability to interpret regulatory updates and provide clear guidance to clients regarding resulting actions or documentation requirements.
  10. Demonstrated ability to independently lead complex pharmaceutical medical writing projects and manage multidisciplinary review teams.
  11. Experience interacting directly with clients and senior stakeholders.
  12. Demonstrated ability to review and provide substantive scientific and regulatory feedback on the work of other senior medical writers.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. 12+ years of total pharmaceutical, biologic, and medical device regulatory medical writing experience.
  2. Previous Director, Associate Director, Senior Manager, Principal Medical Writer, Regulatory Writing Lead, or comparable senior-level experience.
  3. Advanced scientific degree such as MS, PharmD, PhD, MD, or equivalent.
  4. Experience across both U.S. and EU regulatory environments.
  5. Experience with EU MDR remediation or transition projects.
  6. Experience responding directly to Notified Body questions.
  7. Experience leading NDA/BLA submission programs and integrated clinical submission workstreams.
  8. Experience with eCTD Modules 2 through 5.
  9. Experience leading multidisciplinary submission teams.
  10. Experience advising clients on evolving FDA, EU MDR, MDCG, ICH, or other regulatory requirements.
  11. Leadership experience in a medical writing consultancy or CRO supporting multiple external pharmaceutical clients.

title: Senior Maritime Commercial Solutions Consultant
description:
Who we are

Veson Nautical is an established, fast-growing software company. We provide end-to-end logistical, operational, and analytical solutions that make maritime commerce more efficient and effective.

The opportunity

This role puts your shipping experience at the centre of how Veson sells. As an integral member of the sales team, you will help prospects and existing clients envision, architect, and adopt tailored solutions across our multi-product portfolio. Clients trust people who have run chartering desks, voyages, and the systems behind them, and you will bring that credibility to every commercial engagement.

You will drive revenue growth by combining first-hand industry knowledge with technical and functional curiosity, in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment. The role balances sophisticated commercial engagements with firm-building work that multiplies team impact, including sharing how shipping businesses operate with the colleagues around you. You bring the business knowledge, and we will teach you our products and our pre-sales methods.

Who thrives in this role

You have worked in shipping at an owner-operator, an integrated trader, or a comparable company, as a Charterer, an Operator, or a Business Application Manager or Business Process Owner. You are close to the business and comfortable with technology, and you pick up new systems quickly. You are ready to move from using solutions to shaping and selling them.

Responsibilities

Core pre-sales activities
  • Deliver in-depth product demonstrations and presentations tailored to each prospect's business objectives and technical requirements, using real chartering, operations, and voyage scenarios
  • Lead technical evaluations, including proofs of concept, RFPs, and complex solution design across multiple product combinations
  • Develop initial SOWs and Professional Services estimates, validating Veson's deployment capability against customer needs
  • Act as the liaison between sales and the wider Veson organisation for specialised technical assistance
  • Collaborate with Sales, Services, and Product teams to articulate Veson's value proposition, vision, and strategy
  • Build credibility with prospects and clients through demonstrated expertise in both business value and technical implementation
Industry expertise and knowledge sharing
  • Act as the voice of the shipping industry at Veson, translating the realities of chartering, operations, laytime, demurrage, and voyage economics into client conversations and product thinking
  • Share operational and commercial knowledge with the Solutions Consulting team, mentoring colleagues on how owners, operators, and traders work
  • Build and maintain relationships across the shipping community, including owners, operators, charterers, and traders, to open doors and strengthen client trust
Solution design and technical leadership
  • Master the features and functionality across Veson's suite of solutions, including IMOS, Shipfix, CoCaptain AI, Data Lake, and integrations
  • Design and scope integration requirements during the pre-sales stage, articulating technical feasibility and implementation approach
  • Serve as a go-to internal technical resource, educating sales colleagues, clients, and prospects on Veson's offerings
  • Own the sales demonstration and sandbox environments for your region, streamlining and creatively developing crisp demonstration experiences
  • Use deep product knowledge and technical skills to suggest and, where appropriate, develop tailored product solutions
  • Produce polished, buyer-ready solution and implementation documentation, including manuals, guides, designs, and data considerations
Strategic engagement and discovery
  • Conduct strategic discovery using the MEDDPICC methodology to uncover pain points, decision criteria, and business metrics
  • Present to executive stakeholders, communicating business benefits and technical advantages
  • Support the sales team in building and executing account-specific close strategies
  • Use AI tools, particularly Claude, to accelerate preparation, content creation, and knowledge management, and to automate manual work such as turning meeting transcripts into insights and action items
  • Maintain accurate Salesforce records of client and prospect input, opportunity wins, and losses
Firm-building and team contribution
  • Partner with the commercial team, balancing buyer-facing engagements with internal capability-building
  • Contribute to improvements in SC team structure, process optimisation, and knowledge sharing
  • Create reusable content assets, such as Consensus demos, discovery frameworks, and technical documentation, that scale team impact
  • Mentor and provide thought leadership to associate-level colleagues
  • Travel as needed (up to 25%) within your assigned region and occasionally globally
Communications and relationships

Internal
  • Collaborate extensively with Sales, Services, Product Management, and Marketing to design and deliver tailored solutions
  • Provide industry knowledge, technical expertise, and thought leadership to the wider SC team
  • Contribute client and market insights to the Product team for roadmap prioritisation
  • Mentor Associate and Consultant-level colleagues on technical and commercial skills
External
  • Act as a trusted advisor to prospects and clients, engaging technical teams and senior decision-makers
  • Lead solution demonstrations, proofs of concept, workshops, and technical evaluations
  • Represent Veson in regional client-facing activities, including conferences, industry events, and strategic workshops
  • Build credibility through demonstrated expertise in solving business problems
Qualifications

Experience
  • At least seven years of experience in commercial shipping, in a role such as Charterer, Operator, or Business Application Manager or Business Process Owner at an owner-operator, an integrated trader, or a comparable company, or at least seven years of pre-sales, solutions consulting, or technical sales experience in enterprise SaaS
  • A track record of staying close to the business while working with technology, for example owning or shaping how a team uses systems for chartering, operations, or process management
  • Proven success in fast-paced, entrepreneurial environments, ideally supporting multiple products or systems
  • Experience engaging and presenting to senior stakeholders, including across a full sales or negotiation cycle
  • Project management experience
  • Documentation design and creation experience
Technical skills and tools
  • Technical aptitude, or a demonstrated ability to learn quickly, for APIs, cloud architecture, and system integrations
  • Comfortable to proficient with AI tools, particularly Claude
  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office, plus Salesforce, LinkedIn, and demo platforms, or the ability to learn them quickly
  • Hands-on familiarity with voyage management, chartering, or commercial shipping systems, such as IMOS, is highly valued
Attributes
  • Fast learner who independently absorbs new product and technology knowledge
  • Clear, confident written and verbal communicator with a passion for educating clients and colleagues
  • Coachable, detail-oriented, and effective under pressure
  • Collaborative by nature, with a creative, solutions-first approach
  • Highly organised and process-driven, able to balance competing commercial opportunities, internal projects, and firm-building initiatives
Core competencies (demonstrated strength in several)
  • Strategic discovery and qualification (MEDDPICC framework)
  • Value communication and storytelling
  • Demonstration and technical presentation
  • Competitive positioning and objection handling
  • Stakeholder management and influence
  • Technical acumen (APIs, integrations, cloud architecture)
  • AI fluency and productivity
  • Shipping industry knowledge across chartering, operations, or commercial processes
Language requirements
  • Fluent English (required)
  • Proficiency in a regional language, such as Spanish, Greek, or Japanese, is highly desirable, depending on regional assignment

About Veson Nautical
We are a team of multi-cultural, multi-disciplined professionals that are dedicated to making our clients successful and charting a new, innovative course for the commercial marine industry. Veson Nautical employs a staff of extremely capable creators and innovators all focused on meeting the goals of our clients. We invest extensively in employee development and experience to maintain focus and enthusiasm. The Veson Nautical team is made up of a dynamic blend of engineers, artists, sailors, teachers, brokers, bankers, traders, consultants, and customer service experts.
Veson Nautical is a successful, rapidly growing global software company. Our clients are the world’s leading commercial maritime owners, operators and commodity trading companies. Veson’s solutions enable our clients to identify new opportunities and proactively manage their business to make more profitable decisions. With offices in Singapore, Tokyo, London, Athens, Houston and headquarters in Boston, USA, Veson Nautical is a dynamic organization with a committed team of professionals. Dedicated to ensuring the highest levels of client satisfaction, Veson Nautical brings decades of experience, technical knowledge, enthusiasm and commitment to clients around the world. The combination of exceptional market growth and leading market position make this a superb opportunity for the right candidate.

title: Assistant Project Manager
description:
Overview

At Colliers Project Leaders, we deliver capital project solutions to fulfill our clients’ needs across the built environment. The work we do makes a difference in communities and for the people who live there. We have a passion for it.

Our commitment to realizing our clients' vision inspires us to look beyond the immediate – to the possibilities of what we can achieve together. We are 18,000 projects and counting – improving lives and helping shape the growth of sustainable, progressive and inclusive communities.

Your Role

Join our team as an Assistant Project Manager with the Alberta Team in our Edmonton office!

Our Assistant Project Managers get the opportunity work with the best in the industry and to develop their skills on a diverse range of projects that vary in scope and complexity with the Alberta Business unit.

To be successful in this role you will be able to demonstrate experience supporting projects varying in scope and complexity with depth related to fit-up projects, renovation and commercial mixed-use environments.

Responsibilities

  • Work alongside experienced project managers to learn the keys to client satisfaction and successful project delivery
  • Provide project support to the Project Manager(s) including schedule updates, progress reports and preparation of tender and contract documents
  • Engage in on-site organization of contractors and consultants
  • Attend project and site meetings to capture action items
  • Provide a communication path between the Project Manager(s) and contractors, consultants and suppliers
  • Provide relief support on other projects when available to do so
  • Ensure that project activities are conducted in accordance with Colliers Project Leaders Quality Management System

Qualifications

  • A university degree or diploma in engineering, architecture or construction management (or an equivalent combination of academic and practical experience)
  • A minimum of 1 - 3 years of project coordination experience supporting projects of varying size and scope ideally in retail fit-up/renovation & expansion projects and commercial mixed-use environments
  • Actively working towards obtaining the Project Management Professional Designation (PMP) through the Project Management Institute.
  • Previous exposure to consultant and design management, construction contract administration and project financial an asset
  • An understanding of project delivery models, including design-build, construction management, design-bid-build
  • Excellent written and verbal communication and presentation skills
  • A results-oriented approach with the ability to take responsibility
  • Exceptional organizational skills and the ability to prioritize competing tasks to meet tight deadlines
  • Strong computer skills, including a working knowledge of scheduling (MS Project), word processing (Word) and spreadsheet (Excel) software applications

Base Salary pay ranges are determined by role, level, and location and reflects the minimum and maximum target for new hire base salaries for the position. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Annual bonus opportunities are in addition to base salary.

Don’t have every single qualification?

We know that some people are less likely to apply for a job unless they are a perfect match. At Colliers Project Leaders, we’re not looking for “perfect matches.” We’re looking to welcome people to our diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace. So, if you’re excited about this role but don’t have every single qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. Whether it’s this role or another one, you may be just the right candidate.

What you can expect:

  • An opportunity to truly impact our communities
  • A flexible work environment
  • A comprehensive onboarding experience
  • Significant professional development, training, and a mentorship program
  • A paid volunteer day
  • An environment where people feel welcome, heard and included, regardless of their differences
  • And much more!

Join our team of difference-makers and help shape the growth of dynamic communities!

title: Cybersecurity Engineer II
description:
Why Us?

With a mantra of Empowering Human Potential, Hanger, Inc. is the world's premier provider of orthotic and prosthetic (O&P) services and products, offering the most advanced O&P solutions, clinically differentiated programs and unsurpassed customer service. Hanger's Patient Care segment is the largest owner and operator of O&P patient care clinics nationwide. Through its Products & Services segment, Hanger distributes branded and private label O&P devices, products and components, and provides rehabilitative solutions to the broader market. With 160 years of clinical excellence and innovation, Hanger's vision is to lead the orthotic and prosthetic markets by providing superior patient care, outcomes, services and value. Collectively, Hanger employees touch thousands of lives each day, helping people achieve new levels of mobility and freedom.

Could This Be For You?

The Cybersecurity Engineer II is responsible for assessing, securing, and integrating technology environments associated with mergers and acquisitions across Hanger's national network of patient care clinics and business operations. Working across the full deal lifecycle, from pre-close due diligence through Day 1 stabilization and post-close integration, this role performs hands-on security engineering, technical assessments, compromise assessment and threat hunting, remediation, and implementation of enterprise security controls across acquired environments.

The Cybersecurity Engineer II partners with Hanger’s corporate Security leadership team to translate technical findings into clear, business-focused risk reporting that informs deal decisions and integration priorities, and helps ensure that protected health information (PHI) and critical clinical and business systems in acquired companies are brought up to enterprise security and compliance standards.

Your Impact

Due Diligence and Assessment

  • Pre-Close Due Diligence: Support pre-close security due diligence by reviewing target-company security documentation, questionnaire responses, incident and breach history, and external attack surface to identify deal-impacting risks and inform integration planning.
  • Technical Assessments: Perform technical security assessments across on-premises, cloud, and hybrid environments.
  • Compromise Assessment and Threat Hunting: Conduct or coordinate compromise assessments and threat hunting in acquired environments before network interconnection, looking for indicators of compromise, persistence mechanisms, unauthorized or stale accounts, and anomalous authentication activity.
  • Vulnerability Assessment: Conduct vulnerability assessments, coordinate penetration testing of acquired systems, and drive remediation of identified security gaps and misconfigurations.
  • Application and Data Review: Review acquired-company application portfolios to identify business-critical systems (including electronic health record, practice management, and billing platforms), data sensitivity and PHI locations, authentication methods, integrations, and security risks.
  • Third-Party Risk: Inventory and assess acquired-company vendors, business associates, and sub-processors, and identify gaps in Business Associate Agreements and security-related contract terms.

Integration and Remediation

  • Day 1 Controls: Define and implement Day 1 security controls for acquired entities, including enforced multifactor authentication, privileged access cleanup, endpoint protection, email security, and centralized logging.
  • Security Tooling: Deploy, configure, and support enterprise security tooling and controls within acquired environments, including endpoint detection and response, SIEM, identity governance, email security, secure access, and backup platforms.
  • Cloud Hardening: Perform hands-on security hardening of cloud environments, including identity, access controls, network exposure, logging, configuration, and remediation of identified weaknesses.
  • Network Segmentation: Design and validate secure interconnection and segmentation between acquired and enterprise networks, including separation of clinical, corporate, and vendor zones.
  • Platform Integration: Integrate acquired environments with enterprise security platforms, controls, and processes, including security monitoring, vulnerability management, incident response, and identity lifecycle management.
  • Monitoring and Incident Response: Monitor and analyze security events in acquired environments during the integration window, when threat activity is typically elevated, and respond to and investigate incidents, performing initial containment, eradication, recovery, and documentation in coordination with Security Operations.
  • Automation: Use PowerShell, Python, or similar scripting to automate discovery, assessment, and onboarding tasks so that each integration is faster and more consistent than the last.

Risk, Compliance, and Collaboration

  • Risk Reporting: Document technical findings, remediation activities, and residual risks, and produce risk-rated findings, remediation plans with estimated effort and cost, and business-focused summaries for technical, deal team, and leadership stakeholders.
  • Compliance: Assess acquired environments against the HIPAA Security Rule and enterprise frameworks such as NIST CSF 2.0, NIST SP 800-53, and PCI DSS, and support audit and compliance activities through integration.
  • Playbook and Standards: Develop and maintain the M&A security playbook, including diligence questionnaires, assessment runbooks, Day 1 checklists, and integration standards, and contribute to related security policies, standards, and procedures.
  • Collaboration: Collaborate with M&A, Legal, Compliance, Privacy, Security, Identity, Infrastructure, Networking, and acquired-company IT teams to support secure integration.
  • Workforce Onboarding: Support security awareness and onboarding for acquired-company workforces to align them with enterprise security policies and best practices.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Experience: 5+ years of experience in cybersecurity, security engineering, cloud security, or a related field, including hands-on technical assessment and remediation work.
  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent work experience.
  • Identity and Cloud: Hands-on experience securing Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, and cloud environments, including Azure and AWS.
  • Security Tooling: Experience deploying and supporting enterprise security tooling such as endpoint detection and response, SIEM, email security, firewalls, IDS/IPS, vulnerability scanning, and identity governance platforms.
  • Vulnerability Management: Experience identifying and remediating vulnerabilities and security misconfigurations.
  • Must have, or be eligible to obtain, a valid driver’s license and driving record within the standards outlined within Hanger’s Motor Vehicle Safety Policy and Procedures.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, or large-scale technology integrations.
  • Experience with compromise assessments, threat hunting, technical due diligence, or third-party security assessments.
  • Healthcare industry experience, including protecting PHI, securing electronic health record and practice management systems, managing connected medical device risk, and working with Business Associate Agreements.
  • Experience securing enterprise applications and cloud-hosted environments.
  • Experience consolidating identities, endpoints, and email tenants from acquired companies into an enterprise environment.
  • Experience with HIPAA, PCI DSS, ISO/IEC 27001, or SOC 2 control environments.
  • Project management skills and the ability to manage multiple integration workstreams concurrently.
  • Security and Cloud Certifications: CISSP, CCSP, GSEC, Security+, Microsoft SC-500 (Cloud and AI Security Engineer Associate), AWS Certified Security – Specialty, CCSK, or equivalent.
  • Incident Response Certifications: GCIH, GCFA, or equivalent incident handling and forensics certifications.

Additional Success Factors

  • Investigation: Ability to perform log analysis, incident investigation, and threat hunting using monitoring and detection tools.
  • Technical Knowledge: Strong knowledge of identity and access management, endpoint security, cloud security, vulnerability management, network protocols, system hardening, and security architecture fundamentals.
  • Scripting and Automation: Ability to use PowerShell, Python, or similar languages to automate security and identity workflows.
  • Frameworks: Working knowledge of the HIPAA Security Rule and security frameworks such as NIST CSF 2.0 and NIST SP 800-53.
  • Soft Skills: Strong analytical problem-solving abilities; clear written and verbal communication, including translating technical findings for non-technical and executive audiences; sound judgment in handling confidential, time-sensitive deal information; and a teamwork orientation.
  • Travel: Ability to travel to acquired-company and clinic locations as needed.
  • Act with integrity in all ways and at all times, remaining honest, transparent, and respectful in all relationships.
  • Keep the patient at the center of everything that you do, building lifelong trust.
  • Foster open collaboration and constructive dialogue with everyone around you.
  • Continuously innovate new solutions, influencing and responding to change.
  • Focus on superior outcomes, and calibrate work processes for outstanding results.

Pay range of $110,400-$138,000 + bonus + benefits. This pay range is posted to comply with wage transparency laws. Hanger salary ranges vary based on skill, ability, knowledge, geographic location and other variables.

Our Investment in You

  • Competitive Compensation Packages
  • 8 Paid National Holidays & 4 additional Floating Holidays
  • PTO that includes Vacation and Sick time
  • Medical, Dental, and Vision Benefits
  • 401k Savings and Retirement Plan
  • Paid Parental Bonding Leave for New Parents
  • Flexible Work Schedules and Part-time Opportunities
  • Generous Employee Referral Bonus Program
  • Mentorship Programs- Mentor and Mentee
  • Student Loan Repayment Assistance by Location

title: Ombudsman Statutory Director
description:
Paysafe is a global payments platform powering the experience economy, with a strong focus on the iGaming, video gaming, e-commerce, retail, travel and hospitality sectors. With 30 years of expertise in payment technology, Paysafe helps businesses and consumers lift every experience through seamless, secure payment solutions, including card payments, digital wallets such as Skrill, eCash solutions like PaysafeCard, and a suite of local payment methods. With approximately 2,900 employees across 12 countries and annualized transactional volume of $167 billion in 2025, Paysafe connects people and businesses worldwide through innovative digital payment experiences.

Position Overview Paysafe is seeking an experienced and highly independent Ombudsman Statutory Director based in Brazil to support its regulated Brazilian business. Reporting to the Senior Legal Counsel, the successful candidate will act as both the statutory Director responsible for the Ombudsman function and the appointed Ombudsman, ensuring compliance with applicable regulatory requirements and maintaining an effective, independent, and customer-focused complaint resolution framework.

This role combines regulatory oversight, governance responsibilities, customer protection, complaint management, and Board-level reporting. The successful candidate will serve as a key independent control function within the organization and act as a primary point of contact for matters relating to escalated customer complaints, conduct risk, and Ombudsman-related regulatory obligations.

Key Responsibilities
1. Ombudsman & Complaint Resolution
  • Independently review, investigate and resolve escalated and unresolved customer complaints.
  • Ensure all determinations are impartial, fair, objective and supported by appropriate analysis and documentation.
  • Issue clear, well-reasoned and conclusive responses within applicable regulatory timelines.
  • Manage complaints referred by regulatory authorities, consumer protection bodies and other external stakeholders.
  • Ensure that all Ombudsman activities comply with applicable legal and regulatory requirements.
2. Statutory Director Responsibilities
  • Act as the statutory Director responsible for the Ombudsman function before the Central Bank of Brazil and other relevant authorities.
  • Ensure the effectiveness, independence and proper governance of the Ombudsman framework.
  • Maintain oversight of customer complaint management processes and associated control mechanisms.
  • Promote a culture of customer protection, integrity and regulatory compliance throughout the organization.
  • Serve as a senior escalation point for Ombudsman-related regulatory and governance matters.
3. Governance, Risk & Regulatory Oversight
  • Operate as an independent second-line oversight function.
  • Identify systemic issues, conduct risks, customer detriment risks and operational deficiencies arising from complaints.
  • Escalate material risks, significant trends and recurring issues to senior management and the Board of Directors.
  • Provide recommendations for corrective actions and monitor implementation and effectiveness.
  • Support regulatory examinations, audits and inspections related to Ombudsman activities and customer protection matters.
4. Reporting & Board Engagement
  • Prepare and present periodic reports to senior management, the Board of Directors and relevant committees.
  • Report on:
    • Complaint volumes and trends;
    • Root causes and systemic issues;
    • Emerging customer, conduct and regulatory risks;
    • Status of remediation initiatives.
    • Provide actionable recommendations to improve customer outcomes, products, services and internal processes.
  • Ensure appropriate management visibility and governance over customer-related risks.
5. Documentation & Compliance
  • Maintain complete, accurate and audit-ready complaint files and records.
  • Ensure full traceability of investigations, decisions and supporting documentation.
  • Maintain records and evidence required by applicable regulations.
  • Ensure ongoing compliance with all applicable regulatory requirements, including those imposed by the Central Bank of Brazil.
6. Stakeholder Management
  • Work collaboratively with Legal, Compliance, Risk, Operations, Customer Experience and Product teams.
  • Gather relevant information required for complaint investigations and reviews.
  • Challenge business decisions constructively where customer protection, conduct or regulatory concerns arise.
  • Maintain independence while fostering effective cross-functional relationships.

Key Capabilities & Competencies
  • Exceptional judgment and decision-making skills.
  • Strong independence and ability to challenge business decisions when required.
  • High level of integrity, professionalism and ethical conduct.
  • Strong governance and regulatory mindset.
  • Excellent analytical, investigative and problem-solving skills.
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and influencing capabilities.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with senior management, regulators and Board members.

Qualifications & Experience
  • Bachelor’s degree in law, Business Administration, Finance, Public Policy or a related discipline.
  • Advanced degree or relevant professional qualifications preferred.
  • Minimum 4 years of relevant professional experience, including experience in one or more of the following areas:
  • Ombudsman functions;
  • Regulatory compliance;
  • Legal advisory;
  • Consumer protection;
  • Conduct risk;
  • Financial crime risk management;
  • Regulatory affairs;
  • Dispute resolution, mediation or investigations.
  • Experience within financial services, payments, banking or fintech environments strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience interacting with regulators, senior management and governance bodies.
  • Strong understanding of customer complaint frameworks, consumer protection principles, governance structures and regulatory expectations applicable to financial institutions.
  • Ombudsman certification (e.g., FEBRABAN or Associação Brasileira de Ouvidores), or ability to obtain certification within the required timeframe.
  • Fluent Portuguese and English required.
  • Spanish is considered an asset.

title: Houseperson
description:
Location: Four Points by Sheraton Anaheim

JOB SUMMARY

Under supervision, supports daily housekeeping operations by preparing guest rooms for cleaning, removing soiled linens and trash, distributing clean linens and supplies, and assisting Room Attendants in maintaining an efficient room-cleaning process. Performs physically demanding tasks throughout indoor and outdoor areas of the property while maintaining cleanliness, responding to guest requests, and delivering excellent guest service in accordance with Company standards.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

  • Prepares assigned guest rooms for servicing by stripping beds, removing used linens and towels, collecting trash, and clearing designated items to provide Room Attendants with a clean and organized workspace.

  • Works ahead of Room Attendants to ensure guest rooms are properly stripped and prepared for efficient cleaning and timely room turnover.

  • Collects, transports, and properly disposes of trash and debris from guest rooms, housekeeping areas, and designated interior and exterior locations.

  • Collects and transports soiled linens to designated laundry areas, following established procedures for handling and separation.

  • Delivers and distributes clean linens, towels, amenities, and housekeeping supplies to Room Attendants, linen closets, and designated storage areas throughout the property.

  • Assists Room Attendants with room preparation and additional housekeeping tasks as needed to support daily productivity and operational demands.

  • Maintains cleanliness and organization of housekeeping storage areas, linen closets, service corridors, and other assigned areas.

  • Assists with maintaining the cleanliness of interior and exterior public areas, including walkways, stairwells, entrances, and other designated spaces.

  • Responds promptly and courteously to guest requests, including the delivery of towels, linens, amenities, and other requested items.

  • Provides professional, friendly, and attentive guest service during all guest interactions.

  • Safely operates housekeeping carts, linen bins, trash containers, and other equipment used to transport supplies and materials throughout the property.

  • Maintains awareness of room status, operational priorities, and daily housekeeping needs to ensure timely support of Room Attendants.

  • Reports maintenance concerns, damaged equipment, safety hazards, and unusual conditions to the appropriate department.

  • Follows proper procedures for handling and reporting lost and found items.

  • Adheres to all safety guidelines, including proper lifting techniques, safe equipment operation, and appropriate handling of cleaning chemicals and potentially hazardous materials.

  • Regular, reliable attendance and punctuality is a key component of this position.

  • Maintains a professional appearance in accordance with Company standards; wears the appropriate uniform or attire.

  • Maintains open and effective communication with team members and management.

  • Attends and participates in team meetings.

  • Adheres to established safety and emergency procedures and protocols, including Company, federal, and state-specific regulations and guidelines.

  • Completes all required Company training/compliance courses as assigned.

  • Adheres to Company standards and maintains compliance with all policies and procedures.

  • Performs other related duties and responsibilities as assigned.

EDUCATION

  • High school diploma or equivalent preferred.

EXPERIENCE

  • No prior experience or training required.

  • Previous housekeeping, hospitality, or physically demanding work experience preferred.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position does not include any supervisory responsibilities.

LICENSES & CERTIFICATIONS

  • This position does not require licenses or certifications.

SKILLS & ABILITIES

This position requires the ability to understand and follow oral and written directions, communicate effectively with team members and management, and interact professionally with internal and external customers.

  • Strong time management and organizational skills, with the ability to prioritize assignments and complete tasks efficiently.

  • Ability to work independently while supporting Room Attendants and the overall housekeeping team.

  • Ability to maintain a consistent work pace throughout a physically demanding shift.

  • Ability to recognize daily operational priorities and proactively assist with room preparation, linen distribution, and housekeeping needs.

  • Strong teamwork and interpersonal skills, with a willingness to assist others in achieving departmental goals.

  • Ability to respond promptly and professionally to guest requests while maintaining a positive guest experience.

  • Ability to safely operate housekeeping equipment and transport supplies and materials throughout the property.

  • Ability to work effectively in both indoor and outdoor environments.

  • Ability to follow established safety procedures, including proper lifting techniques and safe handling of potentially hazardous materials.

  • Ability to recognize unsafe conditions and report concerns promptly.

  • Ability to work scheduled shifts, follow all timekeeping policies, and comply with federal, state, and local labor regulations, including those related to meal and rest breaks.

  • Ability to perform effectively with frequent interruptions and changing operational priorities.

  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to maintaining Company cleanliness and quality standards.

  • Ability to maintain a positive and professional working environment.

  • Ability to work effectively in a culturally diverse environment and support diversity and inclusion within the organization.

TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS

  • No travel required.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The essential functions of this position require the following physical activities, with or without reasonable accommodation:

  • Standing and Walking: Requires prolonged standing and constant walking throughout the shift, including movement between guest rooms, hallways, laundry facilities, storage areas, and exterior property locations.

  • Bending, Stooping, Kneeling, and Reaching: Requires frequent bending, stooping, kneeling, crouching, and reaching to strip beds, remove trash, handle linens, and complete assigned tasks.

  • Lifting and Carrying: Regularly lifts and carries items weighing up to 25 pounds, with occasional lifting of items weighing up to 50 pounds, including linens, trash, supplies, and equipment.

  • Pushing and Pulling: Frequently pushes and pulls housekeeping carts, linen bins, trash containers, and other equipment throughout the property.

  • Repetitive Motion: Performs repetitive physical movements involving the hands, arms, shoulders, back, and legs throughout the workday.

  • Climbing and Balancing: May be required to navigate stairs, ramps, uneven surfaces, and wet or slippery areas while performing assigned duties.

  • Communication and Awareness: Requires the ability to communicate with guests and team members, follow instructions, and identify potential safety hazards.

  • Physical Workload: This is a physically demanding position requiring sustained activity throughout the shift, with duties performed in both indoor and outdoor environments.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • Indoor and Outdoor Exposure: Regularly works in guest rooms, hallways, laundry areas, storage spaces, and exterior property locations. May be exposed to heat, cold, humidity, rain, and changing weather conditions.

  • Temperature Variations: Exposure to varying temperatures when moving between climate-controlled guest areas, laundry facilities, service corridors, and outdoor spaces.

  • Excessive Noise: May be exposed to elevated noise levels generated by housekeeping equipment, laundry machinery, guest activity, and general hotel operations.

  • Vibrations: Potential exposure to vibrations from carts, machinery, and housekeeping equipment.

  • Biological Hazards: Potential exposure to bodily fluids, contaminated linens, trash, and other materials requiring appropriate protective measures.

  • Chemicals: Potential exposure to cleaning agents, disinfectants, and other chemicals used in housekeeping operations.

  • Atmospheric Conditions: Exposure to dust, odors, fumes, humidity, and varying ventilation conditions in guest rooms, service areas, and exterior spaces.

  • Physical Hazards: Potential exposure to wet floors, uneven surfaces, moving equipment, heavy carts, and other conditions requiring adherence to established safety procedures.

Responsibilities

Are you passionate about advancing maternal and newborn care through data, quality improvement, and clinical excellence? We are seeking a Program Coordinator, Perinatal Services, to lead and support initiatives that drive exceptional outcomes across our Women's and Newborn Services program.

  • Collaborate with physicians, nursing leaders, and frontline staff to implement evidence-based practices and patient safety initiatives.

  • Support staff education by sharing quality data, best practices, and improvement strategies through huddles, skills fairs, meetings, and other educational forums.

Education

• Pay ranges listed are an estimate and subject to change.• If any bonuses are noted, they are only applicable to external hires meeting criteria.

Velkommen til Bioenergy
Du bliver del af Day Ahead Trading, hvor du sammen med dine kolleger får en vigtig rolle i vores daglige handel med el samt i arbejdet med at sikre, at vores handelsaktiviteter lever op til gældende regler, processer og compliancekrav. I vores team arbejder vi sammen om vores fælles mål i en hverdag, hvor videndeling, sparring og hjælpsomhed er en naturlig del af kulturen. Vi tager ansvar for både egne og fælles leverancer og lykkes bedst i flok.

I jobbet vil du:

  • bidrage til optimering af værdien af virksomhedens produktion

  • koordinere og følge op på interne processer, kontroller og governance-aktiviteter
  • bidrage til dialog med interne interessenter inden for Legal og Compliance
  • deltage i projektopgaver relateret til regulatoriske ændringer, procesforbedringer og implementering af nye krav.

For at få succes i denne rolle forventer vi, at du:

  • er en holdspiller, der samtidig arbejder selvstændigt og tager ansvar for egne opgaver
  • har en struktureret og detaljeorienteret tilgang til dit arbejde og er god til at kommunikere og samarbejde på tværs af faglige områder
  • kan bevare overblikket i et miljø præget af højt tempo og skiftende prioriteringer
  • har interesse for/eller erfaring med compliance, regulering og/eller governance
  • har en relevant uddannelsesmæssig baggrund inden for økonomi, finans, jura, statskundskab eller tilsvarende

**For denne stilling er det forventede grundlønsniveau kr. 45.360,- - kr. 68.040,- for lokationen i jobannoncen. Den endelige løn fastsættes på baggrund af relevante kompetencer, erfaring og forventet opfyldelse af rollen inden for det angivne løninterval for at sikre et fair og konkurrencedygtigt tilbud. Forestil dig en fremtid med Ørsted

Bliv en del af verdens førende virksomhed inden for vedvarende energi

Bliv en del af en verdensførende virksomhed inden for vedvarende energi
Ørsted er verdensførende inden for havvind, og vi er en af de største virksomheder i verden inden for vedvarende energi. Hos os er du med til at skabe en verden, der udelukkende kører på grøn energi. Som et af verdens førende selskaber inden for vedvarende energi bygger vi på vores medarbejderes nysgerrighed og passion, når vi innoverer og udvikler nye teknologier eller skalerer eksisterende teknologier, samtidig med at vi samarbejder med regeringer, leverandører og vores industripartnere om at gøre løsninger inden for vedvarende energi til virkelighed. I Ørsted arbejder vi sammen med stor respekt for hinanden, og vi er altid åbne overfor nye perspektiver på, hvordan vi kan løse vores opgaver, uanset hvor store eller små de er.

Om Ørsted

  • Vi leverer bæredygtige, stabile og konkurrencedygtige energiløsninger – herunder havvind, landvind, solenergi og energilagring – til lande, virksomheder og lokalsamfund.
  • Det er vores vision at skabe en verden, der udelukkende kører på grøn energi.
  • Vi byggede verdens første havvindmøllepark, Vindeby i Danmark, i 1991, og i 2022 idriftsatte vi verdens største, Hornsea 2 i Storbritannien.
  • Vi blev grundlagt i Danmark i 2006 og er i dag ca. 8.000 medarbejdere i 15 lande over hele verden – og vi bliver hele tiden flere.

Et inkluderende team

I Ørsted gør vi vores yderste for at være en inkluderende arbejdsplads, hvor du bliver respekteret for den, du er, værdsat for de unikke perspektiver, du bidrager med, og får en fair belønning for de resultater, du opnår. Alle vores medarbejdere har de samme muligheder for at få indflydelse og udvikle sig uanset alder, race, etnicitet, fødested, køn, seksuel orientering eller handicap.

title: Integration Engineer
description:
At Digibee, we aren’t just building technology; we are unlocking the innovation potential of the world’s largest companies bymaking the complex simple.

In an integration market valued at approximately $250 billion, our cloud-native, low-code iPaaS platform empowers every developer to build and monitor end-to-end workflows, eliminating technical debt and accelerating digital transformation.

Why join us?

Founded in Brazil in 2017, we are now a global team distributed across the Americas, driven by a culture of flexibility and autonomy.

Following a $60 million Series B funding round, we are in full global expansion, combining the agility of a startup with the stability of a company backed by major global players.

Here, you don’t just witness growth, you are the engine behind it.

If you seek real impact and want to redefine how the world connects, you belong here.

Let’s simplify the world, one integration at a time.

About the role

The Integration Expert is a strategic consultant who will leverage the Digibee platform to drive projects requiring system integrations, delivering robust and scalable solutions to our clients.

This role involves designing and developing solutions based on our platform, including API development, defining integration architectures with microservices, orchestrating and choreographing services, and decoupling data flows.

  • Solution Analysis and Design
  • Conduct detailed functional analysis with clients and technical stakeholders.
  • Identify requirements, dependencies, risks, and technical constraints.
  • Design scalable and resilient solutions based on modern system-integration patterns.
  • Produce diagrams and/or technical documentation to present the solution to clients clearly.
  • Use Digibee’s AI resources to map flows, detect patterns, and accelerate technical understanding.
  • Digibee Platform Development
  • Build end-to-end integration pipelines using Digibee platform components.
  • Configure authentication, messaging patterns, data manipulation, mappings, and synchronous/asynchronous integrations.
  • Implement observability mechanisms (logs, metrics, tracing) to support operations and troubleshooting.
  • Ensure technical quality, performance, and security of integrations.
  • Leverage Digibee’s AI to accelerate development, automation, and validations.
  • Estimation and Accountability
  • Accurately estimate development effort and pipeline complexity.
  • Communicate deadlines clearly and transparently.
  • Take responsibility for meeting deadlines, ensuring delivery quality, and mitigating risks.
  • Propose alternatives when replanning is required.
  • Communication and Project Management
  • Facilitate technical meetings with internal teams and clients.
  • Maintain clear, objective, and frequent communication on delivery status.
  • Coordinate alignment across teams (CSM, Product, Engineering, Support).
  • Document decisions and ensure all stakeholders remain aligned and informed.
  • Guide clients in adopting the Digibee platform and applying AI to their integrations.
  • Testing and Validation
  • Create and execute functional and integrated test scenarios.
  • Validate end-to-end behavior across all participating systems.
  • Support UAT/validation activities with clients.
  • Ensure quality and reduce rework throughout the project.
  • Use AI to generate test cases, validate contracts, and detect inconsistencies.
  • Support and Troubeshooting
  • Diagnose and resolve incidents in integration pipelines.
  • Use platform logs, metrics, and tracing to identify root causes.
  • Propose preventive improvements and structural fixes.
  • Continuous Improvement and Best Practices
  • Promote integration, governance, and architectural standards within the team.
  • Contribute to internal frameworks, reusable components, and best practices.
  • Support platform evolution and internal process improvements.
  • Act as an ambassador for innovation and AI adoption within projects.
  • Strong experience in system integration, REST/SOAP APIs, messaging, and event-driven architectures.
  • Hands-on experience with the Digibee platform or similar tools (MuleSoft, Boomi, Make, Workato, etc).
  • Proficiency in data manipulation (JSON, XML, CSV), transformation, and mapping.
  • Knowledge of relational and NoSQL databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, ElasticSearch, etc.).
  • Experience with messaging systems (Kafka, SQS, RabbitMQ) and data streaming.
  • Understanding of Cloud Computing, containers, microservices, and distributed architectures (no need to orchestrate Kubernetes, only understand the principles).
  • Experience with Git and version control.
  • Experience with basic CI/CD pipelines for integration governance.
  • Knowledge of observability practices (structured logging, tracing, metrics).
  • Advanced troubleshooting skills in integrations.
  • Advanced English for reading, writing, and conversation (including international client interactions).

title: Director, partner programs
description:
Acumatica sells through partners, so the programs that govern how partners are recruited, paid, certified and held accountable are the go-to-market engine. Acumatica is seeking a leader to own five partner program operations: Value Added Reseller (VAR), Independent Software Vendor (ISV), Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), Services, and Alliance (referral). Over the next 12-24 months you will streamline the program architecture, shift incentives from activity toward growth, adoption and customer outcomes, establish one trusted partner data and attribution model, and scale the ISV and marketplace motion for the AI era. The VAR and ISV programs carry the most revenue and strategic weight and will receive the majority of your investment; OEM, Services and Alliance are held to the same standards of governance, economics and accuracy, with proportionate effort. You will be the single leader accountable for how the programs are structured, measured and operationalized, and how they incent and compensate partners across all five engagements.

You will work closely with our channel, isv, oem and alliance partner management organizations to drive towards measured targets with minimums established by each of the program frameworks. In addition to the frameworks, you will own the compliance, the economics, the data and the infrastructure, and the tools those relationships run on. You will present general proposals for program structure and economics to executive leadership.

You will work closely with the partner recruiting, education and enablement teams to ensure that the established program frameworks provide definitional direction to the development of educational content for use in the enablement motion as well as for partners who are struggling to meet minimum standards or even not live up to their fullest potential. You will stand up tools and reporting mechanisms which support the various functional motions within the organization, including account managers, that will help all parties track and measure partner success and failure.

You will also be responsible for overseeing onboarding and offboarding of partners and your team will lead compliance efforts when partners underperform.

Strong cross-functional leadership is an essential element of success in this role.

This role reports to the SVP, Partner Strategy and Programs.

What you own:

  • Responsibilities Across All Five Programs (VAR, ISV, OEM, Services and Alliance).
  • Each program is in a different stage of maturity. You will design, govern and evolve each program as needed, including standards, eligibility, tiers, benefits, requirements, and operating standards.
  • Own the program roadmap and annual refresh cycle, incorporating partner feedback, competitive benchmarking, financial modeling, executive approval and launch.
  • Maintain consistent internally and externally facing documentation across all programs, including governance documents, program guides, policies, and FAQs.
  • Perform compliance reviews and audits to ensure minimum standards are met and benefits are awarded correctly.
  • Build automation to manage top of funnel prospective partner pipeline and manage initial qualification prior to introducing candidates to the appropriate recruiting team.
  • Manage the operations of partner onboarding and offboarding and interface with legal to ensure proper execution and tracking of legal agreements, amendments and addendums across all programs. This includes transitioning partners between programs on an as needed basis and managing the rules of engagement and the partners participating in multiple programs.
  • Oversee deal attribution, conflict resolution and payment rules across the programs where it applies. Manage the approval workflows and handle exceptions which occur outside of policy.
  • Own program economics—including margins, discounts, incentives, rebates, MDF, referral fees, revenue sharing and contra-revenue—and model the P&L impact of changes before launch. Serve as the approver prior to payment of fees such as MDF and referrals as well as oversee and approve margin exceptions.
  • Manage the incentive lifecycle from modeling and calculation through accrual, documentation, audit, reporting and payment. Partner with Finance on forecasts, payment accuracy, audit readiness and alignment with company margin targets.
  • Equip account managers with scorecards, segmentation, business-plan frameworks and a monthly performance cadence.
  • Maintain a common partner data model and metrics framework across Sales, Finance and Marketing. Report consistently on partner-sourced and partner-influenced revenue, customer attach, partner health, retention, program ROI as well as additional metrics measured for each program.
  • Program-Specific Responsibilities (In addition to responsibilities across all programs)

VAR Program

  • Own the VAR tier, margin and discount architecture and the partner profitability model, so that a well-run VAR earns an attractive return on subscription margin and services.
  • Define and report the productive-partner ratio, partner concentration and time to productivity for new VARs; run an annual portfolio review (invest, fix, exit) with Channel Management.
  • Align VAR incentives to net-new ACV, installed-base expansion, retention and ISV or product attach rather than activity.
  • Define geographic and segment coverage and white-space analysis with Channel Management and RevOps.

ISV Program

  • Partner with the ISV business development team, own admission decisions based on alignment with product strategy and roadmap, market fit and technical quality.
  • Own solution certification standards for architecture, security and privacy, including review, renewal triggers and removal.
  • Govern marketplace listing standards and the listing lifecycle, including quality thresholds and removal of solutions that no longer qualify.
  • Define when referral, resale and revenue-share models apply.
  • Run strategic ISV business reviews against agreed targets and give Account Managers visibility into certified and listed solutions.

Alliance Program

  • Partnering with partner recruiting team, manage and optimize the framework for referring Alliance members, systems integrators, consulting firms and strategic technology alliances, joint business-plan standards, co-sell rules and governance cadence.
  • Manage lead and opportunity tagging, referral fees and payment timing, keeping referral processes simple enough to operate at scale.

General Leadership and Operational Responsibilities

  • Own the ecosystem strategy and multi-year plan, including market coverage, partner mix, priority ISV solution categories, geographic expansion, segment investment and build-versus-partner decisions.
  • Run partner advisory boards and executive sponsor programs, translating feedback into program improvements.
  • Own the partner technology stack, including PRM/portal, CRM, deal registration, certification, marketplace listings, referral tracking and reporting, maintaining one authoritative partner record.
  • Serve as the primary channel counterpart to Finance, FP&A, Revenue Accounting, Deal Desk and Legal; present data-backed program economics and margin decisions to the CRO, CFO and executive/board as required.
  • Build, lead and develop the programs and operations team; set priorities, manage budgets and hold the team accountable for measurable outcomes.
  • Coordinate execution with RevOps, Education, Recruiting, Enablement, Legal and Channel Management.

How success is measured

This role is measured on partner program operations – ability to drive and influence partner growth and volume, customer retention and expansion as well as influenced revenue. Operational excellence: deal-registration approval, onboarding and payment cycle times; scorecard coverage and adoption by Channel Managers; and quarterly compliance and remediation results.

What success looks like:

  • First 90 days: complete a current-state audit of all five programs, baseline the metrics above and agree attribution definitions with Sales, Finance and Marketing.
  • By 12 months: launch a simplified program framework with outcome-based incentives, a single partner data model and a decision-rights matrix adopted by Sales and Finance, and a defined ISV and marketplace roadmap.
  • By 24 months: demonstrate measurable improvement against agreed targets for partner productivity, ISV attach and partner retention, with program cost as a percentage of channel revenue at or below plan.
  • 10+ years in partner programs, channel operations or channel management at a software company; 5+ years leading teams.
  • Demonstrated ownership of VAR or reseller programs, including tier, margin and incentive design, and of and ISV programs.
  • Direct experience running an ISV or technology partner program, including eligibility criteria, solution certification or marketplace listing, and ISV agreements.
  • Proven financial modeling skill: margin, discount and incentive structures, with a track record of presenting them to senior finance leaders and executives.
  • Hands-on command of PRM and CRM platforms and partner reporting. AI and Excel or equivalent analytical fluency.
  • Experience writing and administering partner agreements and program policy, in coordination with Legal.
  • Experience in a company with the majority of revenue through indirect channels, and with services-led partners that implement the product.
  • Experience rationalizing or sunsetting program elements and managing partner change, including grandfathering and communication.
  • Executive communication: board-ready materials, clear written program documentation.
  • Working knowledge of revenue recognition and control considerations for channel incentives (rebates, MDF, referral fees), or the ability to partner effectively with Revenue Accounting.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience designing referral programs and alliance or systems integrator programs.
  • ERP, SaaS or vertical software channel experience.
  • Experience with marketplace or app store platforms, and with technical certification of partner solutions.
  • International or multi-region program experience.
  • Experience in a company with a majority of revenue through indirect channels.
  • Managing the contract negotiation process for redlining a plus.

title: Merchandise Processor Manassas Sudley FT
description:

Partner with retail team members in a high-energy, fast-paced environment to perform a variety of critical inventory management responsibilities. You’ll sort, process, and prepare donated merchandise for display and sale in your own retail store. Our shoppers will love you!

Goodwill offers exciting opportunities for professional growth, and robust benefits, including the option for same day pay, accrued personal time off (PTO), paid holidays, premium pay for working certain holidays, basic life insurance, short/long term disability benefits, individual and family medical, dental and vision benefits, pet insurance, generous employee discounts, and access to an employee assistance program (EAP). 403(b)/401(k) plan with match available after 1 year.

Responsibilities

 Action Oriented Customer Focus Composure Time Management

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

1. Transfers merchandise from containers to determine appropriateness for the sales floor in accordance with established guidelines. 2. Stays abreast of brand name, designer labels, current and vintage styles.3. Prepare items for the sales floor. Evaluate items to determine quality, pricing, value and salability. 4. Counts number of items processed and records on official log.5. Sorts apparel into boutique, salable, and salvage categories according to quota.6. Ability to perform continuous walking, stooping, standing, bending, lifting, kneeling and climbing for prolonged periods of time (up to 7 hours – per 8 hour shift).5.
